a1_01.text: am / is / are - formas del verbo to be
a1_01.note: I am, he is, they are
a1_01.exp:
to be es el verbo más importante del idioma inglés, un análogo del ruso “to be/appear”.

Tres formas: am - sólo con I; is - con él, ella, eso; are - contigo, nosotros, ellos.

⚠️ Una diferencia importante con el ruso: en inglés el verbo no puede faltar. En ruso decimos “soy un estudiante” y en inglés debemos decir: I am a student.
a1_01.exc: Formas cortas: yo soy, tú eres, él es, ella es, es, nosotros somos, ellos son. En respuestas breves está prohibida la abreviatura: Yes, I am. (no Yes, I'm)
mistakes: She be a teacher → She is a teacher
I is hungry → I am hungry
Saltar a ser: I student → I am a student
ex: I am hungry.
Tengo hambre.
She is a doctor.
Ella es doctora.
They are ready.
Están listos.
It is cold today.
Hace frío hoy.

a1_02.note: I'm not tired. He isn't here. They aren't ready.
a1_02.exp:
La negación se construye agregando not: am not, is not, are not.
Formas cortas: isn't (= no es), aren't (= no es). Sólo am not no se reduce a amn't: ¡una excepción!
mistakes: I amn't tired → I'm not tired (¡no existe!)
He don't tired → He isn't tired
She is not = shes not - solo she's not o she isn't
ex: I'm not a student.
No soy un estudiante.
He isn't tired.
No está cansado.
We aren't ready.
No estamos listos.

a1_03.text: Preguntas con ser: Am I? / Is she? / Are they?
a1_03.note: Is she a teacher? Are you cold? Am I late?
a1_03.exp:
En las preguntas, el verbo to be se coloca antes del sujeto: She is → Is she?

Preguntas especiales: palabra interrogativa + to be + sujeto: Where is he? What is this?

Respuestas cortas: Yes, I am. / No, she isn't.
mistakes: Is you cold? → Are you cold?
She is late? - pregunta sin inversión: Is she late?
Where he is? → Where is he?
ex: Are you a student?
¿Es usted un estudiante?
Is it expensive?
¿Es caro?
Where are they?
¿Dónde están?

a1_04.text: Respuestas cortas: Yes, I am. / No, she isn't.
a1_04.note: Sólo forma completa - no permitido: "Sí, lo soy"
a1_04.exp:
En resumen responde el pronombre + to be. No puedes acortar la forma del verbo en una respuesta afirmativa.
Are you tired? — Yes, I am. ✓    Yes, I'm. ✗
mistakes: Yes, I'm → Yes, I am (no se puede abreviar en una respuesta afirmativa)
No, she is'nt → No, she isn't
ex: Is she ready? — Yes, she is.
¿Está lista? - Sí.
Are they your friends? — No, they aren't.
¿Son tus amigos? - No.

a1_05.note: a dog, an apple, an hour, a university
a1_05.exp:
a y an son el artículo indefinido, colocado antes del primer objeto mencionado en singular.

La elección depende del sonido, no de la letra:
• a - antes del sonido consonante: a book, a car, a university [ju...]
• an - antes de un sonido vocálico: an apple, an hour [aʊ...], an honest man
a1_05.exc: a university, a European - aunque empiezan con vocal, el sonido inicial es [j], por tanto a. an hour, an honest - h es mudo, el sonido inicial es una vocal.
mistakes: an university → a university (sonido [j])
a apple → an apple
a honest man → an honest man (h mudo)
ex: I saw a cat in the garden.
Vi un gato en el jardín.
She is an engineer.
Ella es ingeniera.
It took an hour.
Tomó una hora.

a1_06.note: the sun, the door, the book on the table
a1_06.exp:
the se usa cuando el hablante y el oyente saben de qué están hablando.

Cuando ponemos the:
1. El tema ya ha sido mencionado:I saw a cat. The cat was black.
2. Único en su especie: the sun, the moon, the earth
3. Del contexto se desprende claramente: Close the window, please.
4. Superlativo: the best, the biggest
a1_06.exc: Pronunciación: the [ðə] antes de consonantes, [ði] antes de vocales. En el discurso oral, a menudo [ðɪ] para dar énfasis.
mistakes: <s>I like the music</s> → Me gusta la música (significado general - sin artículo)
<s>The life is short</s> → Life is short
He is the doctor → He is a doctor (Primera mención)
ex: The film we saw was amazing.
La película que vimos fue increíble.
Could you pass the salt?
¿Podrías pasar la sal?

a1_07.text: Artículo cero: cuando el artículo no es necesario
a1_07.note: I like music. She plays tennis. He is from Russia.
a1_07.exp:
El artículo no está colocado antes de:
• Nombres propios: John, London, Russia
• Idiomas y nacionalidades: English, Russian
• Deportes y juegos: football, chess
• Alimentos/bebidas en sentido general: I love coffee
• Conceptos abstractos en general: Life is short. Love is blind.
• Plural en sentido general: Dogs are friendly.
mistakes: <s>I play the tennis</s> → I play tennis
<s>She speaks the Spanish</s> → She speaks Spanish
<s>the Russia</s> → Russia (países sin artículo, excepto EE. UU. y Reino Unido)
ex: She speaks Spanish.
Ella habla español.
He plays basketball every day.
Juega baloncesto todos los días.

a1_08.note: I work. He works. She goes. It runs.
a1_08.exp:
El Present Simple se usa para: hábitos y acciones habituales, hechos y verdades generales, horarios.

Fórmula: yo/tú/nosotros/ellos + infinitivo; él/ella/it + infinitivo+s/es

Reglas para escribir terminaciones -s/-es:
• La mayoría de los verbos: + s → works, plays
• Termina en -o, -ch, -sh, -s, -ss, -x: + es → goes, watches, washes
• Termina con consonante + -y: -y → ies → studies, tries
a1_08.exc: Excepciones: have → has, be → is, do → does, go → goes
a1_08.tip: Marcadores de tiempo: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never, every day/week.
mistakes: She work → She works (olvidé -s para la tercera persona)
He go → He goes (go → goes)
She studys → She studies (consonante + y → ies)

markers.note: Los marcadores de frecuencia aparecen antes del verbo principal, pero después de to be.

ex: I drink coffee every morning.
Tomo café todas las mañanas.
She works in a hospital.
Ella trabaja en un hospital.
The Earth goes round the Sun.
La Tierra gira alrededor del Sol.

a1_09.note: I don't like. He doesn't like. (no: he don't)
a1_09.exp:
La negación se construye usando el verbo auxiliar do/does + not:
• Yo/tú/nosotros/ellos + don't + infinitivo
• él/ella/ello + doesn't + infinitivo

⚠️ ¡Después de doesn't el verbo principal sin -s! She doesn't like (no likes).
mistakes: She doesn't likes → A ella no like (después no le gusta, ¡la forma base!)
He don't work → He doesn't work
I not like → I don't like

markers.note: Los mismos marcadores que para las oraciones afirmativas.

ex: I don't eat meat.
No como carne.
He doesn't speak French.
No habla francés.
They don't work here.
No trabajan aquí.

a1_10.note: Do you like pizza? Does he work here? Where do they live?
a1_10.exp:
Preguntas: Do/Does + sujeto + infinitivo?
• I/you/we/they: Do you...?
• he/she/it: Does she...?

Preguntas especiales: palabra interrogativa + do/does + sujeto + infinitivo:
Where does she live? What do they do?

⚠️ Excepción: la pregunta “¿Quién?” sin do: Who likes ice cream?
mistakes: Does she likes? → Does she like?
Do he work? → Does he work?
<s>Where she lives?</s> → Where does she live?

markers.note: En las preguntas, los marcadores van después del tema.

ex: Do you speak Russian?
¿Hablas ruso?
Does she live nearby?
¿Vive ella cerca?
Where do you work?
¿Dónde trabajas?

a1_11.text: Stative verbs: verbos no utilizados en continuo
a1_11.note: I know, not: I am knowing. I love, not: I am loving.
a1_11.exp:
Algunos verbos describen un estado en lugar de una acción; no se usan en tiempos continuos.

Grupos principales:
• Opiniones: know, believe, think, understand, remember, forget
• Sentimientos: love, hate, like, want, need, prefer
• Percepción: see, hear, smell, taste, look
• Ser: be, exist, belong, contain, seem, appear
a1_11.exc: think/have/see/taste se puede usar en Continuo, pero con un significado diferente: I think (opinión) versus I'm thinking (pensando ahora mismo).
mistakes: I am knowing → I know
She is loving him → She loves him
He is wanting a coffee → He wants a coffee
ex: I understand you. (не: I am understanding)
Te entiendo.
She loves chocolate. (не: is loving)
A ella le encanta el chocolate.

a1_12.text: Pronombres personales: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
a1_12.note: Siempre necesitas un tema explícito; no puedes omitirlo.
a1_12.exp:
A diferencia del ruso, en inglésel asunto siempre es obligatorio.
En ruso: “Me voy a casa”. En inglés: I am going home.

Formas de objeto (después de un verbo o preposición): me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
mistakes: Is cold today → It is cold (el tema no se puede omitir)
Me like pizza → I like pizza
She told to him → She told him
ex: She is a teacher.
Ella es profesora.
Tell him the truth.
Dile la verdad.
Can you help me?
¿Puedes ayudarme?

a1_13.text: Adjetivos posesivos: my, your, his, her, its, our, their
a1_13.note: mi libro, su auto, su casa - no cambies por número
a1_13.exp:
Los adjetivos posesivos muestran propiedad y van antes del sustantivo.
Importante: its (sin apóstrofe) = propiedad; it's (con un apóstrofe) = es.

No cambies de género ni de número: my friend / my friends - lo mismo.
mistakes: Its a big house → It's a big house (it's = it is)
The cat hurt it's paw → hurt its paw (es = pertenencia)
Their friends is nice → Their friends are nice
ex: This is my phone.
Este es mi teléfono.
Their dog is cute.
Su perro es lindo.
The cat hurt its paw.
El gato se lastimó la pata.

a1_14.note: cats, boxes, knives, children, men, sheep
a1_14.exp:
Regla básica: añadir -s.

Casos especiales:
• -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -o: + es → boxes, watches, tomatoes
• vocal + -y: + s → boys, days
• consonante + -y: -y → ies → cities, babies
• -f/-fe: → ves → knives, leaves, wives

Irregular: child→children, man→men, woman→women, tooth→teeth, foot→feet, mouse→mice, person→people, fish→fish, sheep→sheep
mistakes: two childs → two children
three mans → three men
boxs → boxes (agregar -es)
ex: one bus → two buses
un autobús → dos autobuses
one child → many children
un hijo → muchos hijos

a1_15.exp:
this (este) - singular + siguiente
these (estos) - plural + cercano
that (ese) - singular + lejano o ya conocido
those (esos) - plural + lejano

También se usa sobre el tiempo: this week (esta semana), that year (ese año).
mistakes: These is my pen → This is my pen
Those are that books → Those are those/the books
That book over here - this (cerca), that (lejos)
ex: This is my bag.
Esta es mi bolsa.
Those shoes are expensive.
Esos zapatos son caros.
What is that?
¿Qué es?

a1_16.note: There is a park. There are five rooms.
a1_16.exp:
La construcción there is/are significa “existe/existe”, “es”.
• There is + sustantivo singular. número
• There are + sustantivo plural. número

Negación: There isn't / There aren't
Pregunta: Is there...? / Are there...?

⚠️ ¡No confundir con it is! There is a book on the table (el libro existe ahí) vs It is a good book (característica).
ex: There is a cinema near here.
Hay un cine cerca.
Are there any shops nearby? — Yes, there are.
¿Hay alguna tienda cerca? - Sí.

a1_17.text: Preposiciones de lugar: in, on, at, under, next to, behind, between
a1_17.note: in the box, on the table, at the station
a1_17.exp:
Tres preposiciones principales:
• in = dentro de algo: in the box, in the city, in bed
• on = en la superficie: on the table, on the wall, on the left
• at = en un punto específico: at the station, at home, at school

Otras: under (debajo), next to/beside (cerca), behind (detrás), in front of (en frente), between (entre), opposite (opuesto)
ex: The keys are on the table.
Las llaves están sobre la mesa.
She is in the kitchen.
Ella está en la cocina.
Meet me at the entrance.
Encuéntrame en la entrada.

a1_18.note: Open your books. Don't run. Please sit down.
a1_18.exp:
Imperativo = forma base de un verbo sin sujeto.
Negación: No + infinitivo
Please hace que la solicitud sea más educada (al principio o al final).

Para incluir al hablante: Vamos + infinitivo → Let's go! Let's eat!
ex: Turn left at the crossroads.
Gire a la izquierda en la intersección.
Don't touch that!
¡No toques esto!
Let's have a break.
Tomemos un descanso.

a1_19.text: puedo / no puedo - habilidad y resolución
a1_19.note: I can swim. She can't drive. Can I help you?
a1_19.exp:
can es un verbo modal, expresa:
1. Habilidad/Habilidad: I can play the guitar
2. Oportunidad: It can be dangerous
3. Resolución (hablada): Can I use your phone?

⚠️ can nunca cambia: he can (no he cans). Después va un infinitivo sin to.
mistakes: Can you to help me? → Can you help (sin hacerlo)
She cans do it → She can do it (puede no cambia)
<s>I can to speak French</s> → I can speak French
ex: I can speak three languages.
Hablo tres idiomas.
She can't come today.
Ella no puede venir hoy.
Can you help me, please?
¿Podrías ayudarme?

a1_20.text: Palabras interrogativas: what, where, who, when, how, why, which, whose, how much/many
a1_20.note: What is this? Where do you live? How old are you?
a1_20.exp:
Las palabras interrogativas aparecen al principio de la pregunta, seguidas de un verbo auxiliar antes del sujeto.

• what = qué/cuál
• where = dónde/dónde
• who = quién (pregunta sin hacer: Who lives here?)
• when = cuándo
• why = por qué
• how = cómo; how much = cuántos (incontables); how many = cuántos (contar); how old = cuántos años; how long = cuánto tiempo
ex: Where does she work?
¿Dónde trabaja?
What time is it?
¿Qué hora es?
How many brothers do you have?
¿Cuantos hermanos tienes?

a1_21.note: one, two, three... twenty-one, a hundred, a thousand
a1_21.exp:
Números 1–12: palabras especiales (uno, dos, tres... doce).
13–19: + -teen (trece, catorce... diecinueve; excepciones: trece, quince, dieciocho).
Decenas: veinte, treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta, sesenta, setenta, ochenta, noventa.
Compuestos: 21 = twenty-one (vía guión).

100 = a/one hundred; 1000 = a/one thousand.
Después de cien/mil - and (BrE): two hundred and fifty.
ex: She is twenty-three years old.
Tiene veintitrés años.
The ticket costs four hundred pounds.
El billete cuesta cuatrocientas libras.

a1_22.note: the first, the second, the third, the fourth... the twenty-first
a1_22.exp:
Los números ordinales se forman sumando -th: fourth, fifth, sixth...
Excepciones: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), fifth (5th), eighth (8th), ninth (9th), twelfth (12th).
Siempre se usa con el artículo the: the first day, the third floor.

Fracciones: ½ = a half, ⅓ = a third, ¼ = a quarter.
ex: My office is on the third floor.
Mi oficina está en el tercer piso.
Today is the first of March.
Hoy es primero de marzo.

a1_23.note: John's car, my sister's friend, the children's toys, the teachers' room
a1_23.exp:
En inglés, la pertenencia se expresa mediante un apóstrofe + s:
• Singular: Tom's book, the dog's tail
• Plural con -s: solo apóstrofo: the teachers' room, my parents' house
• Plural irregular: 's: the children's playground, men's clothes
• Nombres que terminan en -s: James's / James' - ambas opciones son correctas
ex: This is Anna's laptop.
Esta es la computadora portátil de Anna.
The children's toys are in the box.
Juguetes para niños en una caja.

a1_24.text: Preposiciones de movimiento: to, into, out of, up, down, along, across, through
a1_24.note: go to school, walk into the room, run across the street
a1_24.exp:
• to = dirección a un punto: go to work, walk to the park
• into = movimiento hacia adentro: come into the room, jump into the pool
• out of = movimiento hacia afuera: get out of the car, take out of the bag
• up/down = arriba/abajo: climb up the hill, walk down the stairs
• along = a lo largo: walk along the river
• across = a través/a través: swim across the lake, walk across the road
• through = a través: drive through the tunnel
ex: She walked into the room.
Ella entró en la habitación.
He ran across the street.
Cruzó la calle corriendo.
We drove through the forest.
Condujimos por el bosque.

a2_01.exp:
Past Simple: una acción completada en el pasado con o sin un tiempo específico.

Reglas para escribir la terminación -ed:
• La mayoría de los verbos: + ed → worked, played
• Terminan en -e: + d → loved, used
• Consonante + -y: -y → ied → studied, tried
• Una vocal + una consonante (sílaba acentuada corta): duplicar la consonante → stopped, planned
a2_01.tip: Marcadores: yesterday, last week/year, ago, in 2010, at 5 o'clock.
mistakes: She is going to school every day → She goes (hábito = Presente simple)
I am going to the cinema tomorrow - tal vez, pero I'm going to see a film más precisamente con intención
He is wanting → He wants (stative verb)

tags: in the morning (de un día específico)
markers.note: Regla clave: tiempo específico en el pasado → ¡Pasado simple, no presente perfecto!

ex: She worked all day yesterday.
Trabajó todo el día ayer.
They played tennis last Sunday.
Jugaron al tenis el domingo pasado.

a2_02.exp:
Es necesario aprender de memoria unos 200 verbos irregulares. Los 50 más frecuentes cubren ~90% de los usos.

Grupos por similitud de cambios:
• AAA (no cambiar): cut, put, hit, set, let
• ABA (volver al principio): run→ran→run, come→came→come
• ABC (todos diferentes): go→went→gone, be→was/were→been
mistakes: She goed → She went
I buyed → I bought
They didn't went → No go (después de hacerlo - forma básica)

markers.note: Palabra interrogativa ¿cuándo? siempre requiere Pasado Simple (no Presente Perfecto).

ex: I went to Paris last summer.
Fui a París el verano pasado.
She saw a great film.
Ella vio una gran película.
We had a meeting at 9.
Teníamos una reunión a las nueve.

a2_03.note: She didn't go (no: didn't went). I didn't see him.
a2_03.exp:
Negación: didn't (= no) + infinitivo para todas las personas.
⚠️ Después de didn't - forma base del verbo (¡no en tiempo pasado!): She didn't go (no went).
mistakes: I didn't went → I didn't go
She didn't came → She didn't come
Did she played? → Did she play?
She didn't came → She didn't come
What he did? → What did he do?
ex: I didn't see him yesterday.
No lo vi ayer.
She didn't come to work.
Ella no se presentó a trabajar.

a2_04.text: Pasado simple - preguntas: ¿Lo hiciste? ¿A dónde fue ella?
a2_04.note: Did they arrive? What did he say?
a2_04.exp:
Pregunta: ¿Did + sujeto + infinitivo?
Preguntas especiales: ¿Dónde/Cuándo/Qué + did + sujeto + infinitivo?

⚠️ Excepción: la pregunta “¿Quién realizó la acción?” se construye sin hizo: Who called? Who broke the vase?
mistakes: I will to go → I will go (sin hacerlo)
<s>She wills come</s> → She will come (la voluntad no cambia)
I think she go tomorrow → she will go

markers.note: La voluntad se utiliza para decisiones espontáneas, promesas, predicciones sin evidencia.

ex: Did you enjoy the film?
¿Te gustó la película?
Where did they go?
¿A dónde fueron?
Who told you that?
¿Quién te dijo esto?

a2_05.text: was/were - verbo to be en pasado
a2_05.exp:
Tiempo pasado del verbo to be:
• was - con yo, él, ella, it
• were - contigo, nosotros, ellos

Negación: wasn't / weren't
Pregunta: Was she...? Were they...?
mistakes: I am going to will do - sólo una cosa: I'm going to do
She is going to does → she is going to do
<s>He gonna do</s> - forma coloquial, inaceptable por escrito

markers.note: ir a = una decisión o predicción preestablecida basada en signos visibles.

ex: I was very tired last night.
Anoche estuve muy cansado.
They were at home all day.
Estuvieron en casa todo el día.
Was it expensive?
¿Fue caro?

a2_06.note: I'll call you back. It will rain tomorrow. I'll have the pasta.
a2_06.exp:
will se utiliza para:
1. Decisiones espontáneas (tomada en el momento del discurso): I'll help you with that.
2. Predicciones sin un plan específico: I think it will rain.
3. Promesas: I won't tell anyone.
4. Solicitudes: Will you open the window?

Abreviatura: 'll. Negación: won't (= will not).
mistakes: I will to go → I will go (sin hacerlo)
<s>She wills come</s> → She will come (la voluntad no cambia)
ex: The phone is ringing. — I'll get it!
El teléfono está sonando. - ¡Yo responderé!
It will be cold tomorrow.
Mañana hará frío.

a2_07.text: yendo a - intenciones y predicciones obvias
a2_07.note: I'm going to visit Paris. Look out — you're going to fall!
a2_07.exp:
going to se utiliza para:
1. Decisiones e intenciones preestablecidas: I'm going to start a diet next week.
2. Predicciones con signos visibles: Look at those clouds: it's going to rain!

Forma: am/is/are + going to + infinitivo
a2_07.exc: will vs going to: "I'll have coffee" - Estoy decidiendo ahora mismo; "I'm going to have coffee" - Ya lo decidí antes.
mistakes: She is going to does → She is going to do
<s>I am going to will do</s> - no puedes tener dos futuros
ex: I'm going to study medicine.
Voy a estudiar medicina.
She's going to have a baby.
Ella está esperando un bebé.

a2_08.note: She is reading now. They are playing outside.
a2_08.exp:
Present Continuous es una acción que tiene lugar ahora mismo o temporalmente durante este período.

Forma: am/is/are + verbo + -ing

Reglas para escribir -ing:
• La mayoría: simplemente + ing → working, playing
• Termina con -e: eliminar -e + ing → making, coming
• Sílaba acentuada corta: duplicar la última consonante → running, sitting
a2_08.tip: Marcadores: now, at the moment, currently, this week/month.
mistakes: I was visit → I was visiting
She were working → She was working (she/he/it → was)
At 8 I was work → I was working

markers.note: Estos marcadores indican acción en este momento o una situación temporal.

ex: I am studying English right now.
Estoy estudiando inglés ahora.
She's working from home this month.
Ella está trabajando desde casa este mes.

a2_09.text: Presente continuo para el futuro planificado
a2_09.note: I'm meeting Tom tomorrow. We're flying to Rome on Friday.
a2_09.exp:
Presente continuo se utiliza para acuerdos específicos en el futuro, cuando el tiempo y el lugar ya han sido determinados.

Diferencia:
• I'm meeting Alice tomorrow - la reunión ha sido acordada (un plan específico)
• I'll meet Alice tomorrow - intención o propuesta
mistakes: I'm meeting Tom in next week → meeting Tom next week (sin entrar)
We are flying to Rome on the Friday → on Friday

markers.note: Presente Continuo para el futuro - acuerdos específicos, hay un momento y un lugar.

ex: I'm having dinner with Alex tonight.
Esta noche cenaré con Alex.
They're getting married in June.
Se casarán en junio.

a2_10.text: Present Simple vs Present Continuous: diferencia
a2_10.note: I drink coffee (hábito) vs I am drinking coffee (ahora mismo)
a2_10.exp:
Present Simple: hábitos, hechos, horarios, verdades generales.
Present Continuous: algo que está sucediendo ahora mismo o temporalmente.

Comparar:
• She speaks French. - conoce el idioma (siempre)
• She is speaking French. - habla ahora mismo

⚠️ Verbos estátivos (saber, amar, querer, entender...) - ¡sólo presente simple!
mistakes: I am drink coffee every morning → I drink (hábito)
She knowing French → She knows French
Water is boiling at 100°C → Water boils (hecho)

markers.note: El marcador determina la elección: now/at the moment → Continuous; always/every day → Simple.

ex: Water boils at 100°C. (факт)
El agua hierve a 100°C.
I'm reading a great book this week. (временно)
Estoy leyendo un gran libro esta semana.

a2_11.text: debería / no debería - consejos y recomendaciones
a2_11.note: You should see a doctor. You shouldn't eat so much.
a2_11.exp:
should expresa un consejo leve u opinión personal. Más débil que must.
Después de should - infinitivo sin to.

También se usa para criticar o arrepentirse: You should have called (debería haber llamado).
mistakes: You should to see a doctor → should see (sin hacerlo)
She should goes → She should go
I should have went → I should have gone
ex: You should exercise more.
Deberías hacer más ejercicio.
She shouldn't work so hard.
Ella no debería trabajar tan duro.

a2_12.text: debe / no debe - obligación y prohibición estricta
a2_12.note: You must wear a seatbelt. You mustn't smoke here.
a2_12.exp:
must - una obligación fuerte (a menudo interna) o un requisito categórico.
mustn't - una prohibición estricta (¡absolutamente imposible!).

⚠️ Diferencia importante: mustn't ≠ don't have to!
• mustn't = prohibido
• don't have to = no es obligatorio, pero es posible
mistakes: You mustn't to smoke → mustn't smoke
I must to do this → I must do this (sin hacerlo)
You mustn't come ≠ “no necesitas” es “¡no puedes!” Para "no es necesario": don't have to
ex: You must show your passport.
Debes presentar tu pasaporte.
You mustn't smoke here.
No puedes fumar aquí.

a2_13.note: I have to work late. She doesn't have to come.
a2_13.exp:
have to - una necesidad debido a reglas externas, circunstancias o requisitos de otras personas.

Diferencia de must:
• must - necesidad interna: I must call her (yo mismo lo considero necesario)
• have to - externa: I have to wear a uniform (regla)

don't have to=opcional (no es necesario, pero está permitido).
mistakes: <s>I have to can do this</s>: no puedes tener dos modales seguidos
She doesn't have to don't come → She doesn't have to come
<s>You must not to come</s> → mustn't come
ex: I have to finish this report by Friday.
Tengo que presentar mi informe antes del viernes.
You don't have to come if you don't want to.
No tienes que venir.

a2_14.text: podría - habilidad pasada y solicitudes educadas
a2_14.note: She could swim when she was 5. Could you help me?
a2_14.exp:
could es el tiempo pasado de can. Dos significados principales:
1. Habilidad en el pasado: I could read at 4 years old.
2. Solicitudes educadas (más educadas de lo que can): Could you pass the salt, please?

También para la posibilidad actual: It could be true.
mistakes: She could to swim → She could swim (sin hacerlo)
Can I when I was a child → I could when I was a child
<s>Could you to speak slowly?</s> → Could you speak slowly?
ex: She could play the violin as a child.
Sabía tocar el violín cuando era niña.
Could you speak more slowly, please?
¿Podrías hablar más despacio?

a2_15.exp:
Monosilábicos y disilábicos en -y: + er (rápido→más rápido, feliz→más feliz).
Polisilábicos: more + adjetivo.

Reglas de escritura: -e → + r (nice→nicer); sílaba acentuada corta: doble (grande → más grande); -y → ier (pesado→más pesado).

Irregular: good→better, bad→worse, far→further/farther, much/many→more
Después del comparativo - than: She is taller than her sister.
mistakes: She is more tall than → She is taller than
He is more better → He is better
She is tallest in class → She is the tallest
ex: This film is more interesting than that one.
Esta película es más interesante que eso.
Today is worse than yesterday.
Hoy es peor que ayer.

a2_16.note: the biggest, the most beautiful, the best
a2_16.exp:
Monosilábico: the + -est. Polisilábico: the most.
Las reglas de escritura son las mismas que para el grado comparativo.

Irregular: good→the best, bad→the worst, far→the furthest, much/many→the most

⚠️ ¡Siempre con el artículo the! Después de superlativos, a menudo in o of: the tallest girl in the class.
mistakes: He is most clever → He is the most clever / the cleverest
She is the most best → She is the best
This is most interesting film → the most interesting film (necesita)
ex: This is the most expensive restaurant in the city.
Este es el restaurante más caro de la ciudad.
He is the best player on the team.
Es el mejor jugador del equipo.

a2_17.note: I have some money. Do you have any? I don't have any.
a2_17.exp:
some - en oraciones afirmativas y en ofertas/solicitudes.
any - en preguntas y negaciones.

Excepción: some en preguntas cuando esperamos una respuesta afirmativa u ofrecer algo: Would you like some tea? Can I have some water?
mistakes: I have some money? (pregunta) → Do I have any money?
I don't have some cash → I don't have any cash
Would you like any tea? → Would you like some tea? (oferta)
ex: I bought some bread and some milk.
Compré pan y leche.
Is there any milk in the fridge?
¿Hay leche en el frigorífico?
I don't have any cash on me.
No tengo efectivo conmigo.

a2_18.text: much / many / a lot of / a few / a little
a2_18.note: mucha agua (incontable), mucha gente (contable), mucha - en todas partes
a2_18.exp:
much - con incontables (mucha agua, mucho tiempo, mucho dinero).
many - con contables (muchas personas, muchos libros, muchas veces).
a lot of / lots of - con ambos, estilo conversacional.

a few - un poco (contable, neutral/positivo).
few - pocos, casi ninguno (contable, negativo).
a little - un poco (incontable, neutral).
little - poco, casi nada (incontable, negativo).
mistakes: Much people → Many people (contables)
Many money → Much money (incontable)
A few water → A little water
ex: I don't have much time.
No tengo mucho tiempo.
She has a few friends in London.
Tiene varios amigos en Londres.
There is a little sugar left.
Queda algo de azúcar.

a2_19.note: agua, información, consejos - no permitido: un agua, dos consejos
a2_19.exp:
Contables: se pueden contar, hay plurales. número: a book, two books.
Incontable: no se puede contar directamente, no hay plural. números, sin artículo indefinido.

Incontables típicos: water, milk, bread, rice, money, information, advice, news, weather, luggage, furniture, hair, music, work

Para indicar porciones: a glass of water, a piece of advice, a loaf of bread, a bag of rice
mistakes: Two advices → Two pieces of advice (consejos incontables)
An information → Some information
Three furnitures → Three pieces of furniture
ex: Can I have some information, please?
¿Puedo saber algo?
She gave me very useful advice.
Ella me dio consejos muy útiles.

a2_20.text: Preposiciones en / en / en por tiempo
a2_20.note: in March, in 2024, in winter; on Monday, on 5 June; at 3pm, at night
a2_20.exp:
at → hora exacta: at 6 o'clock, at noon, at midnight, at night, at the weekend (BrE)
on → días y fechas: on Monday, on 5 March, on my birthday, on New Year's Day
in → periodos: in July, in 2023, in the morning/afternoon/evening, in summer, in the 21st century

Sin preposición: esta/última/siguiente + hora: this morning, last week, next year
mistakes: at Monday → on Monday
in 8 o'clock → at 8 o'clock
on the morning → in the morning
in my birthday → on my birthday
ex: The meeting is at half past three.
Reunión a las cuatro y media.
She was born on the 12th of April.
Nació el 12 de abril.
I started this job in October.
Comencé este trabajo en octubre.

a2_21.text: para / desde / hace - duración y comienzo
a2_21.note: for three years, since 2020, three years ago
a2_21.exp:
for - duración (cuánto tiempo): for two hours, for a week, for years. Usado con diferentes tiempos.
since - momento inicial (desde): since Monday, since 2019, since I was a child. Usado con el Presente Perfecto.
ago - hace tiempo a partir de ahora: three days ago, a month ago. Sólo con pasado simple.
mistakes: <s>I've been here since three years</s> → for three years
I saw him since Monday → I saw him on Monday (hace con Pasado simple, ¡no desde entonces!)
Three days before → Three days ago
ex: I've been here for six months.
Llevo aquí seis meses.
She's worked here since 2020.
Trabaja aquí desde 2020.
I saw him two days ago.
Lo vi hace dos días.

a2_22.text: Preguntas de cola: ...isn't it? / ...do you? / ...haven't they?
a2_22.note: It's cold, isn't it? You like jazz, don't you?
a2_22.exp:
Las preguntas de etiqueta se utilizan para confirmar o aclarar.

Regla: oración afirmativa → etiqueta negativa, y viceversa.
Verbo auxiliar en la cola = tiempo de la oración principal.

Entonación: ↘ (caída) = confirmación; ↗ (en ascenso) = pregunta real.
mistakes: It's cold, isn't he? → isn't it
She can swim, can't he? → can't she
You don't like it, don't you? → do you? (oración negativa → cola positiva)
ex: It's a nice day, isn't it?
Buen día, ¿verdad?
You don't like horror films, do you?
No te gustan las películas de terror, ¿verdad?
She can swim, can't she?
Ella sabe nadar, ¿no?

a2_23.note: I've got a car. Have you got a pen? She hasn't got time.
a2_23.exp:
have got es una forma coloquial británica de posesión. Valor = have.

• Afirmación: I have got / I've got a laptop.
• Negación: I haven't got / I don't have
• Pregunta: Have you got...? / Do you have...?

⚠️ have got se usa solo en presente. En el pasado, sólo had.
mistakes: I've got a car in 2010 → I bought a car in 2010 (solo tengo el presente)
She had got a dog → Ella had un perro (pasado - solo tenía)
ex: I've got two brothers.
Tengo dos hermanos.
Have you got the time?
¿No sabes qué hora es?
She hasn't got any cash.
Ella no tiene efectivo.

a2_24.text: Adverbios de manera: quickly, carefully, well, hard, fast
a2_24.note: She sings beautifully. He works hard. She drives fast.
a2_24.exp:
La mayoría de los adverbios se forman a partir de adjetivos + -ly: quick → quickly, careful → carefully, slow → slowly.

Casos especiales:
• good → well (no goodly)
• fast → fast (no fastly)
• hard → hard (no hardly - esta es otra palabra: “apenas”)
• late → late (no lately - esto es “últimamente”)

Lugar: generalmente después del verbo/objeto: She speaks English well.
mistakes: She sings beautiful → She sings beautifully
He works hardly → He works hard (apenas = apenas)
She drives fastly → She drives fast
ex: He explained it clearly.
Lo explicó claramente.
She ran fast.
Ella corrió rápido.
They worked hard all day.
Trabajaron duro todo el día.

a2_25.text: Adverbios de frecuencia y su lugar en una oración.
a2_25.note: siempre, generalmente, a menudo, a veces, raramente, nunca - antes del verbo principal
a2_25.exp:
Adverbios de frecuencia: always, usually, often, sometimes, occasionally, rarely, seldom, never.

Colocar en una oración:
• Antes del verbo principal: She always drinks tea.
• Después del verbo to be: He is always late.
• Después del verbo auxiliar: She has never been to Italy.

Además: every day/week, once a week, twice a month - al final de la oración.
mistakes: She always is late → She is always late (after to be)
He drinks always coffee → He always drinks coffee (antes del verbo principal)
<s>She has never been always on time</s>: dos adverbios juntos son inapropiados
ex: I usually wake up at 7.
Normalmente me levanto a las 7.
She is never late for work.
Ella nunca llega tarde al trabajo.
They meet once a week.
Se reúnen una vez por semana.

a2_26.text: Orden de los adjetivos antes de los sustantivos.
a2_26.note: a lovely small old red Italian leather bag
a2_26.exp:
Cuando aparecen varios adjetivos delante de un sustantivo, se observa un orden estricto: Opinión → Tamaño → Edad → Forma → Color → Origen → Material → Propósito
(Opinión → Tamaño → Edad → Forma → Color → Origen → Material → Propósito)

Ejemplo: a beautiful small old square brown French wooden writing desk
mistakes: <s>a wooden French old small bag</s> → orden: tamaño → edad → origen → material
a beautiful Italian big car → gran beautiful auto italiano (tamaño antes de opinión - no)
ex: a lovely little old cottage
encantadora casita antigua
a big red Italian sports car
Gran coche deportivo italiano rojo.

b1_01.note: I have seen it. She has gone. They have arrived.
b1_01.exp:
Present Perfect = have/has + V3 (tercera forma del verbo).

Tres significados principales:
1. Experiencia de vida (sin hora especificada): I have visited Tokyo.
2. Resultado en el presente: I have lost my keys. (ahora no hay llaves)
3. Acción inconclusa, en curso ahora: She has lived here for 5 years.

V3 verbos regulares = Pasado simple (trabajado, jugado). Los incorrectos deben conocerse por separado.
b1_01.tip: Marcadores: ever, never, already, yet, just, recently, lately, so far.
mistakes: I have seen him yesterday → I saw him yesterday (ayer = Pasado simple!)
She has went → She has gone
I have been to Rome last year → I went to Rome last year

markers.note: Nunca usado con un tiempo específico del pasado (yesterday, last year, in 2020 → Past Simple).

ex: Have you ever eaten sushi?
¿Alguna vez has comido sushi?
I've just finished my homework.
Acabo de terminar mi tarea.
She hasn't called yet.
Ella no ha llamado todavía.

b1_02.text: alguna vez / nunca / ya / todavía / sólo - Marcadores Presente perfecto
b1_02.note: Have you ever...? I've never... I've already... Not yet. I've just...
b1_02.exp:
ever - algún día (en preguntas sobre experiencia). Ubicación: frente a V3.
never - nunca (valor negativo). Ubicación: frente a V3.
already: ya (antes de lo esperado). Lugar: antes de V3 o al final.
yet - ya/todavía. En preguntas (¿Ya terminaste?) y negaciones (aún no terminé). Lugar: final de frase.
just - justo ahora. Ubicación: frente a V3.
mistakes: Have you ever been to Paris yet? → ever en la pregunta, yet al final
I've already not finished → I haven't finished yet
I just have eaten → I have just eaten (justo antes de V3)

markers.note: siempre/nunca - antes de V3; ya - antes de V3 o al final; todavía - sólo al final.

ex: Have you ever been to Scotland?
¿Has estado en Escocia?
I've never eaten snails.
Nunca he comido caracoles.
I've already seen that film.
Ya he visto esta película.
She hasn't replied yet.
Ella aún no ha respondido.

b1_03.text: Present Perfect vs Past Simple: la diferencia clave
b1_03.note: I've been to Paris (experiencia) vs I went to Paris in 2019 (hora específica)
b1_03.exp:
Esta es una de las diferencias más importantes en la gramática inglesa.

Present Perfect - conexión con el presente, el tiempo NO está indicado:
I've lost my wallet. (ahora no tengo billetera; esto es importante)

Past Simple: pasado completo, el tiempo está indicado o implícito:
I lost my wallet yesterday. (ayer es un momento específico)

⚠️ Con marcadores de tiempo específicos (ayer, la semana pasada, en 2020, hace) → ¡Solo pasado simple!
mistakes: I have seen him last week → I saw him last week (hora específica = Pasado simple)
Did you ever eat sushi? → Have you ever eaten sushi?
I met him and he has told me → he told me (en un contexto del pasado)

markers.note: Si hay un momento específico (yesterday, in 2020, last year) → Pasado simple únicamente.

ex: I've met the new director. (он сейчас здесь, это актуально)
Conocí al nuevo director.
I met him last Tuesday. (конкретное время)
Lo conocí el martes pasado.

b1_04.text: Presente perfecto con for y since
b1_04.note: I've lived here for 5 years / since 2019.
b1_04.exp:
for - duración: for two days, for a year, for a long time, for ages
since - punto de partida: since Monday, since I was a child, since 2015

La pregunta "¿Cuánto tiempo?" — Cuánto tiempo + Presente perfecto: How long have you known her?
mistakes: I've lived here since five years → for five years
She's known him for 2019 → she's known him since 2019
How long did you live here? → How long have you lived here? (en curso ahora)

markers.note: por + periodo de tiempo; desde + punto de partida. Ambos se utilizan con el Presente Perfecto (Simple y Continuo).

ex: She's worked here for ten years.
Lleva diez años trabajando aquí.
I've known him since university.
Lo conozco desde la universidad.

b1_05.text: Present Perfect Continuous: have been + V-ing
b1_05.note: I have been waiting for an hour. She has been studying all day.
b1_05.exp:
Present Perfect Continuous = haber/ha sido + V-ing

Énfasis en la duración o carácter incompleto de la acción. Responde a la pregunta "¿Cuánto tiempo?"
A menudo explica el resultado visible en el presente: You look tired — have you been running?

Diferencia con el presente perfecto simple:
• I've read 50 pages. - resultado, integridad
• I've been reading all evening. - énfasis en el proceso
mistakes: I've been learning since three hours → for three hours
I've been read all evening → I've been reading
<s>I've been know her for years</s> → saber - verbo estativo, usa Presente Perfecto Simple

markers.note: El Presente Perfecto Continuo enfatiza la duración más que el resultado.

ex: I've been learning English for two years.
Llevo dos años aprendiendo inglés.
Why are your hands dirty? — I've been fixing the car.
¿Por qué tienes las manos sucias? — Estaba reparando el auto.

b1_06.note: I was reading at 8pm. They were talking all evening.
b1_06.exp:
Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing

Valores:
1. Acción en proceso en un momento concreto del pasado: At 9pm I was having dinner.
2. Actividad de fondo interrumpida por otra: I was walking when it started to rain.
3. Acciones paralelas: While she was cooking, he was watching TV.
mistakes: She was walk → She was walking
They was talking → They were talking
I was work at 9pm → I was working

markers.note: while/as → fondo (Past Continuous); when → evento (Past Simple).

ex: It was raining when I left home.
Estaba lloviendo cuando salí de casa.
What were you doing at 7 yesterday?
¿Qué hacías ayer a las 7?

b1_07.text: Past Simple vs Past Continuous: antecedentes y evento
b1_07.note: While I was cooking, he called. I was walking when it started to rain.
b1_07.exp:
Diseño típico: acción de fondo larga (Pasado continuo) + evento corto (Pasado simple).

Sindicatos:
• when: usado con el pasado simple para el evento: She was sleeping when the alarm went off.
• while/as - usado con Pasado Continuo como fondo: While I was watching TV, the power went out.
mistakes: While I cooked, he called → While I was cooking, he called (fondo = Continuo)
I was walking when it was starting to rain → when it started (evento = Pasado simple)

markers.note: while + Past Continuous (fondo) + when + Past Simple (evento).

ex: She was having a bath when the phone rang.
Estaba bañándose cuando sonó el teléfono.
While he was giving his speech, someone fell asleep.
Mientras pronunciaba su discurso, alguien se quedó dormido.

b1_08.text: Tipo 0: Si + Presente, Presente - hechos y leyes
b1_08.note: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils.
b1_08.exp:
Escriba cero: para hechos científicos, leyes de la naturaleza, verdades generales. Ambas acciones siempre suceden juntas.

Forma: If + Present Simple, Present Simple
En lugar de if puedes usar when: When you mix red and blue, you get purple.
mistakes: If you heat water, it will boil → boils (tipo cero - Presente + Presente)
When you mix them, you will get → you get
ex: If you heat ice, it melts.
Si calientas hielo, se derrite.
If it rains, the streets get wet.
Si llueve, las calles se mojan.

b1_09.text: 1er tipo: Si + Presente simple, voluntad - futuro real
b1_09.note: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
b1_09.exp:
Una situación real y probable en el futuro.

Forma: Si + Presente simple, voluntad + infinitivo
⚠️ En la parte if - ¡NUNCA Futuro! Sólo presente simple.

En lugar de will en la parte principal puedes: can, may, might, should.
Las partes se pueden cambiar: I'll stay home if it rains. (sin coma)
mistakes: If it will rain → If it rains (¡NO hay voluntad en la parte si!)
If she will study hard, she passes → If she studies, she will pass
ex: If she studies hard, she'll pass the exam.
Si estudia bien, aprobará el examen.
If you need help, I can come.
Si necesitas ayuda, puedo ir.

b1_10.text: Tipo 2: Si + Pasado simple, sería - presente irreal
b1_10.note: If I had a car, I would drive to work. If I were you...
b1_10.exp:
Una situación irreal o improbable en el presente o futuro.

Forma: Si + Pasado simple, sería + infinitivo
⚠️ ¡El verbo en la parte if es pasado simple, pero el significado es presente/futuro!
⚠️ were se usa para todas las personas: If I were you, If she were here es un estándar de lenguaje formal.
mistakes: If I would have a car → If I had a car
If I was you → If I were you (formalmente)
I would can do it → I could do it (no puedes tener dos modales)
ex: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
Si me ganara la lotería, viajaría por el mundo.
If I were taller, I'd play basketball.
Si fuera más alto, jugaría baloncesto.

b1_11.text: Tipo 1 vs Tipo 2: real versus improbable
b1_11.note: If I win (primero, de verdad) vs If I won (segundo, poco probable)
b1_11.exp:
La elección del tipo reflejatu confianza en la realidad de la situación.

• If I see her (primer tipo) - Espero verla
• If I saw her (segundo tipo): poco probable o simplemente estoy fantaseando

Esta no es una diferencia en la gramática, sino una diferencia en la actitud del hablante.
mistakes: Confusión de tipos 1 y 2: If I win (real) vs If I won (improbable)
If I won, I will buy → no se pueden mezclar: would buy
ex: If it rains tomorrow, I'll take an umbrella. (реально возможно)
Si mañana llueve, llevaré un paraguas.
If it rained every day, I'd move to Spain. (маловероятная фантазия)
Si lloviera todos los días me mudaría a España.

b1_12.text: Passive Voice — Present Simple: is/are + V3
b1_12.note: Coffee is grown in Brazil. The car is made in Germany.
b1_12.exp:
La voz pasiva se utiliza cuando:
• La acción en sí es importante, no la persona que la realiza
• Artista desconocido u obvio

Forma Presente Pasivo Simple: am/is/are + V3
El artista (si es necesario) se agrega con by: The window was broken by the ball.
mistakes: Coffee is grew in Brazil → Coffee is grown
The letter wrote in French → The letter is written
English spoke here → English is spoken
ex: English is spoken in many countries.
En muchos países se habla inglés.
The letter is written in French.
La carta está escrita en francés.

b1_13.text: Passive Voice — Past Simple: was/were + V3
b1_13.note: The bridge was built in 1890. They were arrested.
b1_13.exp:
Pasado Simple Pasivo: was/were + V3
• was - unidades. numero
• were - plural. numero

Activo → Pasivo: Someone stole my car. → My car was stolen.
mistakes: The bridge was build in 1890 → was built
They was arrested → They were arrested
The car stolen → The car was stolen
ex: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889.
La Torre Eiffel fue construida en 1889.
Three people were injured in the accident.
En el accidente resultaron heridas tres personas.

b1_14.text: Passive Voice — Present Perfect: has/have been + V3
b1_14.note: The car has been repaired. All invitations have been sent.
b1_14.exp:
Present Perfect Passive: has/have been + V3

Se utiliza cuando el resultado en el presente es importante y no cuando sucedió exactamente.
mistakes: The project has been complete → has been completed
It have been sent → It has been sent
All guests have been inform → have been informed
ex: The project has been completed.
El proyecto está completo.
All the guests have been informed.
Todos los invitados han sido notificados.

b1_15.note: "I am tired." → He said he was tired.
b1_15.exp:
Cuando se traduce al estilo indirecto, los tiempos verbales se “desplazan” hacia atrás:
• Present Simple → Past Simple: "I work" → he said he worked
• Past Simple → Past Perfect: "I went" → she said she had gone
• Present Perfect → Past Perfect: "I've seen" → he said he had seen
• will → would; can → could; is → was; am going → was going
mistakes: He said he is tired → He said he was tired (cambio de hora)
She told that she was late → She told me/us/him that... (decir requiere un objeto)
He said me that → He told me that / He said that
ex: She said: 'I am leaving.' → She said she was leaving.
Ella dijo que se iba.
He told me: 'I can't come.' → He told me he couldn't come.
Dijo que no podía venir.

b1_16.note: "Where do you live?" → She asked where I lived.
b1_16.exp:
En preguntas indirectas:
1. Sin inversión (orden de las palabras como en la declaración)
2. Ningún auxiliar hizo/hizo
3. Preguntas generales (Sí/No) → si/si + sujeto + verbo
mistakes: She asked where do I live → she asked where I lived (¡sin inversión!)
He asked me what was I doing → what I was doing
She asked if was I tired → if I was tired
ex: "Where do you work?" → She asked where I worked.
Ella me preguntó dónde trabajaba.
"Are you married?" → He wanted to know if I was married.
Quería saber si estaba casada.

b1_17.text: decir vs contar en discurso indirecto
b1_17.note: Él dijo que... / Él me dijo que... - ¡después de decir que necesitas una cara!
b1_17.exp:
say - sin la adición requerida: She said she was tired.
tell - SIEMPRE con un agregado (a quien se le dice): She told me she was tired.

❌ He told that he was late. ✓ He said that he was late.
mistakes: He told that he was late → He said that / He told me that
She said me the news → She told me the news
They told about the problem → They talked about it / said something about it
ex: She said she needed help.
Ella dijo que necesitaba ayuda.
He told us the meeting was cancelled.
Nos informó que la reunión fue cancelada.

b1_18.note: I enjoy reading. She finished writing. He avoided making mistakes.
b1_18.exp:
Estos verbos requieren un gerundio (V-ing) después de ellos:
enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest, keep, consider, deny, imagine, miss, practise, risk, admit, delay, dislike, fancy, give up, involve, put off, recommend, resist

Truco de memorización: si puedes reemplazarlo con "proceso", lo más probable es que sea un gerundio.
mistakes: I enjoy to swim → I enjoy swimming
She finished to write → She finished writing
He avoided to make → He avoided making
ex: I enjoy swimming in the sea.
Me gusta nadar en el mar.
She's considering moving abroad.
Está pensando en mudarse al extranjero.
He avoided making eye contact.
Evitó el contacto visual.

b1_19.note: I want to go. She decided to stay. He managed to finish.
b1_19.exp:
Estos verbos requieren un infinitivo con to:
want, decide, hope, plan, manage, agree, promise, refuse, fail, expect, offer, learn, need, afford, arrange, attempt, choose, claim, demand, deserve, help, pretend, tend, threaten
mistakes: She decided going → She decided to go
He wants going out → He wants to go out
I hope seeing you → I hope to see you
ex: She decided to quit her job.
Ella decidió dejarlo.
I hope to see you soon.
Espero verte pronto.
He failed to answer.
No pudo responder.

b1_20.text: Verbos con ambos (like, love, hate, start, begin)
b1_20.note: Me gusta leer = Me gusta leer - ligera diferencia
b1_20.exp:
Después de like/love/hate/prefer ambas opciones son posibles:
• V-ing: hablamos de la acción en su conjunto: I love cooking. (en general, me gusta cocinar)
• to-inf - estamos hablando de un caso concreto: I'd like to cook tonight.

Después de start/begin/continue/cease prácticamente no hay diferencia.
mistakes: I'd like cooking tonight → I'd like to cook tonight (caso específico)
She started to working → Empezó a working o to work
ex: I love travelling / to travel.
Me gusta viajar.
She started working / to work here in May.
Ella empezó a trabajar aquí en mayo.

b1_21.note: I used to play football. She used to have long hair.
b1_21.exp:
used to: acciones o condiciones habituales en el pasado que ya han cesado.

Forma: usado + infinitivo
Denegación: didn't use to
Pregunta: Did you use to...?

⚠️ ¡No existe el tiempo presente! No puedes: I use to por el momento.
Diferencia de be used to: I am used to waking up early = Estoy acostumbrado (ahora).
mistakes: I use to play football → I used to play
Did you used to...? → ¿Solías use to...? (después de hizo - forma base)
I used to living there → I used to live (infinitivo sin to+ing)
ex: I used to smoke, but I stopped.
Solía ​​fumar, pero lo dejé.
Did you use to play an instrument?
¿Has tocado algún instrumento antes?

b1_22.text: Oraciones relativas: who, which, that, where, whose
b1_22.note: The man who called. The book that I read. The place where we met.
b1_22.exp:
who - para personas: The woman who called is my sister.
which - para objetos y animales: The book which I borrowed was great.
that - para personas y objetos (en cláusulas definitorias): The car that he bought is new.
where - para lugares: The café where we met is closed.
whose - accesorio: The girl whose bag was stolen...

En el habla coloquial, a menudo se omite un pronombre si es un objeto: The film (that) I saw...
mistakes: The man which called → the man who called (quién para las personas)
The place who we met → the place where we met
The girl who's bag → the girl whose bag
ex: The man who lives next door is very friendly.
El señor que vive al lado es muy amable.
The hotel where we stayed had a pool.
El hotel en el que nos alojamos tenía piscina.

b1_23.text: Conjunciones de contraste: although, however, despite, in spite of, whereas
b1_23.note: Although it was raining, we went out. Despite the rain, we went.
b1_23.exp:
although / even though / though + cláusula subordinada.
despite / in spite of + sustantivo / gerundio (¡NO cláusula subordinada!).
however + nueva oración (después de punto o punto y coma).
whereas es un contraste entre dos hechos.
mistakes: Despite it was raining → Despite the rain / Despite raining (sustantivo/gerundio!)
Although the rain, we went → Although it was raining (aunque + frase)
ex: Although she was tired, she kept working.
Aunque estaba cansada, siguió trabajando.
Despite the rain, he cycled to work.
A pesar de la lluvia, fue en bicicleta al trabajo.
It was expensive. However, it was worth it.
Fue caro. Aun así, valió la pena.

b1_24.note: I'll be working at 9 tomorrow. She'll be flying over the Atlantic.
b1_24.exp:
Future Continuous = will be + V-ing

Valores:
1. Una acción que estará en progreso en un momento específico en el futuro: At this time tomorrow, I'll be lying on the beach.
2. Acción planificada y esperada en el futuro (curso natural de los acontecimientos): I'll be seeing her tomorrow anyway.
3. Preguntas educadas sobre los planes (sin presión): Will you be coming to the party?
mistakes: I'll be work at 9 → I'll be working
She will working → She will be working

markers.note: A menudo se utiliza para preguntas educadas sobre planes: Will you be using the car?

ex: Don't call at 8 — I'll be having dinner.
No llames a las 8, cenaré.
This time next week I'll be sitting on a beach.
La semana que viene a esta hora estaré sentado en la playa.

b1_25.note: By Friday I will have finished the report. By 2030 they will have built the bridge.
b1_25.exp:
Future Perfect = will have + V3

Una acción que se completará antes de cierto punto en el futuro.
Usado a menudo con by (the time), before: By the time you arrive, I will have cooked dinner.
mistakes: By Friday I will finish → I will have finished (se completará antes de la fecha límite = Future Perfect)
I'll have finish by Sunday → I'll have finished

tags: by the end of the week
by the end of the year
markers.note: by (the time) es un marcador clave: la acción se completará ANTES de este momento.

ex: I'll have finished this book by Sunday.
Terminaré de leer este libro el domingo.
By 2050, scientists will have found a cure.
Para 2050, los científicos encontrarán una cura.

b1_26.text: Metas subordinadas: to, in order to, so that, so as to
b1_26.note: I study hard to pass. She left early so that she could catch the train.
b1_26.exp:
to / in order to / so as to + infinitivo - meta. In order to y so as to son un poco más formales.
so that + sujeto + verbo - propósito con otro sujeto o con un modal.

⚠️ Negación: in order not to / so as not to (no to not).
mistakes: I study hard for passing → I study hard to pass
She left early for that she could catch the train → so that she could
In order to not upset him → in order not to upset him
ex: She studies hard in order to get a scholarship.
Ella estudia mucho para conseguir una beca.
He left early so that he could catch the last train.
Salió temprano para tomar el último tren.

b1_27.note: give up, look up, turn off, find out, get on, put off, carry on
b1_27.exp:
Verbos compuestos = verbo + partícula (preposición o adverbio). El significado suele ser idiomático.

Los más frecuentes:
• give up = rendirse, rendirse
• find out = descubre, descubre
• turn on/off = encender/apagar
• look up = buscar (en el diccionario/Internet)
• look after = cuidar
• put off = posponer
• carry on = continuar
• get on/along = llevarse bien (con alguien)
• bring up = educar; sacar el tema
• come across = tropezar con
mistakes: She gave up to smoke → She gave up smoking
I looked up the word in → I looked it up (pronombre entre verbo y partícula)
ex: I've given up smoking.
Dejé de fumar.
Can you look after my cat while I'm away?
¿Puedes cuidar a mi gato mientras estoy fuera?
We need to find out what happened.
Necesitamos descubrir qué pasó.

b2_01.note: By the time she arrived, he had already left.
b2_01.exp:
Past Perfect: una acción que se completó antes de otro momento o evento en el pasado.

Forma: had + V3 para todas las caras.
Negación: hadn't + V3
Pregunta: ¿Tenía + sujeto + V3?

Conjunciones típicas: before, after, when, by the time, already, just, never
mistakes: When I arrived, she already left → she had already left
He had never see snow → He had never seen snow
I had went → I had gone

markers.note: El Pasado Perfecto muestra que una acción pasada ocurrió ANTES de otra.

ex: When I arrived, she had already left.
Cuando llegué, ella ya se había ido.
He had never seen snow before that winter.
Nunca había visto nieve antes de ese invierno.

b2_02.text: Past Perfect Continuous: had been + V-ing
b2_02.note: He had been waiting for two hours when she arrived.
b2_02.exp:
Past Perfect Continuous = had been + V-ing
Énfasis en la duración de una acción que ocurrió antes de otro punto en el pasado.
A menudo explica una causa o un resultado visible en el pasado.
mistakes: She was exhausted — she had been work → she had been working
How long had you waiting? → How long had you been waiting?

tags: for two hours when she arrived
markers.note: Énfasis en la duración hasta un momento en el pasado. A menudo explica la causa de la afección.

ex: She was exhausted — she'd been working all night.
Estaba agotada; había trabajado toda la noche.
How long had you been waiting before she arrived?
¿Cuánto tiempo esperaste antes de que ella llegara?

b2_03.text: debe tener + V3 - conclusión segura sobre el pasado
b2_03.note: Ella debe haberlo olvidado. - Estoy seguro de que esta es la única explicación.
b2_03.exp:
must have + V3 = Estoy seguro de que esto sucedió (la única explicación lógica).

Escala de confianza:
• must have done - es casi seguro que sucedió
• should have done: se esperaba que sucediera
• may/might have done - puede haber sucedido
• can't have done; probablemente no sucedió
mistakes: She must forgot → She must have forgotten
He must have leave early → He must have left
You must be exhausted yesterday - en el pasado: must have been
ex: You must have been exhausted after that journey.
Debes estar muy cansado después de este viaje.
She must have left early — her coat is gone.
Al parecer se fue temprano: le faltaba el abrigo.

b2_04.text: no puedo tener + V3 - imposibilidad en el pasado
b2_04.note: She can't have said that! He can't have been there.
b2_04.exp:
can't have + V3 = Estoy seguro de que esto no sucedió (es imposible).
Lo contrario de must have done.
mistakes: She can't forgot that → She can't have forgotten
<s>He couldn't have been there</s> - ¡es cierto! no puedo tener = imposibilidad; no podría tener = oportunidad
ex: He can't have seen her — she was abroad.
No pudo verla: estaba en el extranjero.
That can't have been the right address.
Esta no puede ser la dirección correcta.

b2_05.text: debería tener + V3 - reproche y arrepentimiento
b2_05.note: I should have called. You shouldn't have said that.
b2_05.exp:
should have + V3 = hubiera estado bien hacerlo, pero no lo hice (arrepentimiento, reproche).
shouldn't have + V3 = no debería haberlo hecho.

Esta es una construcción muy común para expresar arrepentimiento y crítica.
mistakes: I should called her → I should have called
She shouldn't have went → She shouldn't have gone
You should have study → You should have studied
ex: I should have brought an umbrella.
Debería haber cogido un paraguas.
She shouldn't have told him the secret.
No debería haberle contado el secreto.

b2_06.text: podría / podría haber + V3 - posibilidad en el pasado
b2_06.note: She might have forgotten. It could have been worse.
b2_06.exp:
might/could have + V3 = esto puede haber sucedido (no lo sabemos con seguridad).

Además: could have done = podría haberlo hecho (pero no lo hizo): I could have won if I had tried harder.
mistakes: She might forgot → She might have forgotten
He could have win → He could have won
ex: She might have forgotten about the meeting.
Quizás se olvidó de la reunión.
He could have left through the back door.
Podría haber salido por la puerta trasera.

b2_07.text: 3er tipo de condicional: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3
b2_07.note: If I had studied harder, I would have passed.
b2_07.exp:
Una situación irreal en el pasado: estamos hablando de algo que no sucedió.

Forma: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3

Ambos elementos son irreales:
• Condición no cumplida
• Tampoco hubo resultados
mistakes: If I studied harder, I would have passed → Si had studied... (3er tipo - ¡Pasado perfecto!)
If she had taken medicine, she would recovered → she would have recovered
ex: If she had taken the medicine, she would have recovered.
Si tomara el medicamento, mejoraría.
If he hadn't left early, he would have met her.
Si no se hubiera ido temprano, la habría conocido.

b2_08.note: If I had studied, I would be fluent now. (pasado → presente)
b2_08.exp:
Los condicionales mixtos conectan diferentes planes de tiempo:

1. Condición pasada → resultado presente:
Si + Pasado perfecto, sería + infinitivo
If I had taken that job, I would be in New York now.

2. Condición actual → resultado pasado:
If + Past Simple, would have + V3
If she were more careful, she wouldn't have broken it.
mistakes: <s>If I had studied, I would be fluent yesterday</s> - tipo mixto sobre el pasado → presente, no el pasado
If she were careful, she didn't break it → she wouldn't have broken it
ex: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
Si hubiera estudiado para ser médico, ahora sería médico.

b2_09.text: Futuro Pasivo y Pasivo con modales
b2_09.note: It will be done. It must be fixed. It should be checked.
b2_09.exp:
Modal + Pasivo: modal + be + V3
• will be done - se hará
• must be done - debe hacerse
• should be done - debe hacerse
• can be done - se puede hacer
mistakes: The report will published → will be published
It must done → It must be done
It should be do → It should be done
ex: The report will be published tomorrow.
El informe se publicará mañana.
This mistake must be corrected immediately.
Este error debe corregirse inmediatamente.

b2_10.note: I had my hair cut. She got her car fixed.
b2_10.exp:
tener/obtener + objeto + V3: usted solicita un servicio o alguien hace algo por usted.

Comparar:
• I cut my hair. - Me corto el pelo yo mismo (lo cual no es típico)
• I had my hair cut. - cortado por un peluquero

get es un poco más conversacional, have es un poco más formal.
mistakes: I cut my hair at the hairdresser → I had my hair cut
She got her car to fix → She got her car fixed
ex: I need to have my teeth checked.
Necesito que un médico me revise los dientes.
She had her house painted last spring.
La primavera pasada pintó la casa (contratando trabajadores).

b2_11.text: Passive reporting verbs: It is said that... / He is believed to...
b2_11.note: It is thought that prices will rise. She is known to be honest.
b2_11.exp:
Dos opciones de construcción con los verbos say, think, believe, report, know, expect, consider:

1. It + pasiva + that + cláusula subordinada: It is believed that...
2. Sujeto + es +V3+ a-infinitivo: She is believed to be...

Utilizado en noticias y textos oficiales.
mistakes: It is said that prices will risen → will rise
He is believed to being honest → He is believed to be honest
ex: It is reported that three people were injured.
Se reportaron tres personas heridas.
He is thought to have left the country.
Se cree que abandonó el país.

b2_12.text: recordar / olvidar + V-ing vs to-inf - diferencia de significado
b2_12.note: I remember locking it (hecho del pasado) vs Remember to lock it (tarea)
b2_12.exp:
remember/forget + V-ing - sobre un evento pasado que recordamos/olvidamos.
remember/forget + to-inf - sobre la tarea: recuerda hacer algo en el futuro.
mistakes: I remember to lock it (si el hecho ya pasó) → I remember locking it
Remember locking it! (tarea) → Remember to lock it!
I forgot doing the homework (si no la has hecho) → I forgot to do the homework
ex: I remember meeting her at a conference. (это было)
Recuerdo haberla conocido en una conferencia.
Remember to call your mother! (нужно сделать)
¡No olvides llamar a tu mamá!
I forgot to buy milk. (не сделал)
Me olvidé de comprar leche.

b2_13.text: stop / regret / mean + V-ing vs to-inf
b2_13.note: Ella dejó de fumar vs Ella dejó de fumar
b2_13.exp:
stop + V-ing: detener la acción.
stop + to-inf - detenerse para hacer otra cosa.

regret + V-ing - lamentar el pasado.
regret + to-inf - lamento informarle (formalmente): I regret to inform you...

mean + V-ing - significa: This means working harder.
mean + to-inf - intención: I meant to call you.
mistakes: She stopped to smoke (si dejó de fumar) → She stopped smoking
She stopped smoking to answer (se detuvo para) → She stopped to answer
ex: He stopped smoking last year.
Dejó de fumar el año pasado.
She stopped to look at the view.
Se detuvo para admirar la vista.

b2_14.text: deseo + Pasado simple - deseo de cambiar el presente
b2_14.note: I wish I knew the answer. I wish I had more time.
b2_14.exp:
wish + Past Simple: sobre un deseo poco realista en el presente.
La forma es la misma que en el segundo tipo de condicional. Para to be - were (formalmente), aunque también se usa was.
mistakes: I wish I know the answer → I wish I knew
I wish I was taller - tal vez, pero formalmente: I wish I were taller
I wish I would know - con haría solo sobre los demás: I wish you would listen
ex: I wish I spoke better English.
Es una pena que no hable mejor inglés.
She wishes she lived in a warmer country.
A ella le gustaría vivir en un país más cálido.

b2_15.text: deseo + Pasado perfecto - arrepentimiento por el pasado
b2_15.note: I wish I had studied harder. I wish I hadn't said that.
b2_15.exp: wish + Past Perfect: arrepentimiento por eventos pasados que no se pueden cambiar. La forma es como en el tercer tipo de condicional.
mistakes: I wish I didn't say that → I wish I hadn't said (arrepentimiento del pasado = Pasado perfecto)
I wish she had took that job → she had taken
ex: I wish I hadn't eaten so much.
Es una pena haber comido tanto.
She wishes she had taken that job offer.
Desearía haber aceptado esa oferta de trabajo.

b2_16.text: deseo + haría - deseo de cambiar el comportamiento de otra persona
b2_16.note: I wish you would stop talking. I wish it would warm up.
b2_16.exp:
wish + would: irritación debido al comportamiento de otra persona o el deseo de cambiar la situación.
⚠️ No puedes usar sobre ti mismo: I wish I would - solo sobre otras personas o el clima/situación.
mistakes: I wish I would stop (sobre mí) → ¡no puedes! Uso: I wish I could stop
I wish you stop talking → I wish you would stop
ex: I wish you would listen to me.
Ojalá me escucharas.
I wish it would stop raining.
Ojalá dejara de llover.

b2_17.note: The man who called (determina cuál) vs My brother, who called, (agrega información)
b2_17.exp:
Definir (definir): sin comas - aclaran de quién/de qué están hablando. El pronombre se puede sustituir por that. No se puede eliminar sin perder el significado.

Sin definición: con comas: agrega información sin cambiar el significado. That no se puede utilizar. Se puede quitar.

⚠️ which en no determinantes puede referirse a la oración completa: She passed the exam, which surprised everyone.
mistakes: My brother, that called, is a doctor → My brother, who called (no puedes usar eso en uno que no sea definitorio)
<s>The man who lives next door, is very kind</s> → sin coma (cláusula definitoria)
ex: The film that I told you about is on tonight. (какой именно)
La película de la que te hablé se proyecta esta noche.
My sister, who lives in Paris, is visiting next week. (доп. инфо)
Mi hermana, que vive en París, llegará la próxima semana.

b2_18.note: the person I work with / the person with whom I work (formalmente)
b2_18.exp:
En el habla coloquial, la preposición viene al final: the house I grew up in.
En el habla escrita/formal, la preposición delante de which/whom: the house in which I grew up.

Después de la preposición - sólo which (para cosas) y whom (para personas). ¡Nunca that!
mistakes: The house which I grew up in it → extra it
The person which I spoke → the person I spoke to
ex: The project I'm working on is fascinating. (разг.)
El proyecto en el que estoy trabajando es muy interesante.
The project on which I am working is fascinating. (форм.)

b2_19.text: Conjunciones de consecuencia: so... that, such... that, therefore, as a result
b2_19.note: It was so cold that we stayed inside. She worked hard; therefore, she passed.
b2_19.exp:
so + adjetivo/adverbio + eso: He spoke so quickly that nobody understood.
tal + (a/an) + adjetivo + sustantivo + eso: It was such a long film that I fell asleep.

Conectar palabras de resultado (entre oraciones): therefore, consequently, as a result, hence, thus.
mistakes: It was so cold that we stayed - ¡verdad! Pero: It was such cold that → Era un a cold day
<s>Such was great his relief</s> → Tan grande fue su alivio (con adjetivo - so)
ex: It was such a good book that I read it twice.
El libro fue tan bueno que lo leí dos veces.
She missed the deadline; consequently, she lost the contract.
No cumplió con el plazo; Como resultado, perdió su contrato.

b2_20.text: estar acostumbrado / acostumbrarse a + V-ing - hábito (real)
b2_20.note: I'm used to waking up early. She's getting used to the cold.
b2_20.exp:
be used to + V-ing / noun = estar acostumbrado (ya acostumbrado).
get used to + V-ing / noun = acostumbrarse (el proceso de acostumbrarse).

⚠️ No confundir con used to + infinitivo (hábitos pasados).
• I used to live in Paris. - vivía (ya no)
• I am used to living in big cities. - acostumbrado a vivir en grandes ciudades
mistakes: I'm used to wake up early → I'm used to waking up (be used to + V-ing)
I get used to woke up → I get used to waking up
ex: I'm not used to getting up so early.
No estoy acostumbrado a levantarme tan temprano.
It took time, but she got used to the new system.
Le llevó tiempo, pero se acostumbró al nuevo sistema.

b2_21.text: Future in the Past: would / was going to
b2_21.note: She said she would call. He was going to leave.
b2_21.exp:
Future in the Past: construcciones que expresan el futuro desde el punto de vista del pasado. Utilizado en discurso indirecto y narrativa.

• would + V (de will): She said she would come.
• was/were going to + V: He was going to call but forgot.
• was about to + V: She was about to leave when he arrived.
mistakes: She said she will come → She said she would come (cambio de hora)
He was going to called → He was going to call
ex: She promised she would be there.
Ella prometió que vendría.
He was about to leave when she called.
Estaba a punto de irse cuando ella llamó.

b2_22.text: ser a - cita oficial y orden
b2_22.note: You are to report by Monday. They were never to meet again.
b2_22.exp:
be to + infinitivo: órdenes oficiales, eventos planificados y destino en la narrativa.

1. Instrucción legal: Passengers are to remain seated.
2. Plan oficial: The summit is to take place next month.
3. Destino en la narrativa: They were never to meet again.
mistakes: You be to submit → You are to submit
She was be never to meet → She was never to meet
ex: You are to submit the report by Friday.
Debe enviar su informe antes del viernes.
She was to become one of the greatest scientists of her time.
Estaba destinada a convertirse en una de las más grandes científicas.

b2_23.text: debería - deber moral y expectativa lógica
b2_23.note: You ought to apologise. She ought to have told us.
b2_23.exp:
ought to es una obligación moral o expectativa lógica. Un should más fuerte.
Siempre con to: ought to go (en contraposición a debería).
Para el pasado: ought to have + V3 - reproche o arrepentimiento.
mistakes: You ought apologise → You ought to apologise (¡siempre deberías hacerlo!)
She ought have told us → She ought to have told us
ex: You ought to apologise for what you said.
Deberías disculparte por lo que dijiste.
She ought to have told us earlier.
Debería habernos dicho antes.

b2_24.note: You needn't worry. / She doesn't need to come.
b2_24.exp:
need como modal (formal, en preguntas/negaciones) y como verbo regular.

Modal (sin -s, sin to):
• You needn't worry. / Need I explain?

Necesidad regular + de:
• She doesn't need to come.
mistakes: <s>You needn't to worry</s> → You needn't worry (modal no tiene por qué estar sin hacerlo)
She need come → She needs to come (necesidad regular + hacerlo)
ex: You needn't fill in both forms.
No es necesario completar ambos formularios.
She doesn't need to attend every meeting.
No es necesario que asista a todas las reuniones.

b2_25.note: How dare you! I daren't ask. She dared to challenge him.
b2_25.exp:
dare - atrévete, atrévete. Modal en preguntas retóricas y negaciones.

Modal: How dare you! / I daren't ask. / Dare I say...
Normal: She didn't dare to look. / He dared to challenge the boss.

⚠️ I dare say = quizás, probablemente (expresión estable).
mistakes: <s>How dare you to say</s> → How dare you say (después de atreverte sin hacerlo)
I dare say it es normal; I dare say = tal vez
ex: How dare you speak to me like that!
¿Cómo te atreves a hablarme así?
She dared to express her opinion openly.
Se atrevió a expresar abiertamente su opinión.

b2_26.note: I hurt myself. She did it herself. They enjoyed themselves.
b2_26.exp:
myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves.

1. La acción se dirige hacia el sujeto: He cut himself.
2. Énfasis (solo, sin ayuda): I did it myself.

Estable: by myself = solo; help yourself = ayúdate a ti mismo.
mistakes: She taught her to play (si ella misma) → She taught herself to play
They enjoyed themself → They enjoyed themselves
I did it by my own → I did it by myself
ex: She taught herself to play the guitar.
Ella aprendió por sí misma a tocar la guitarra.
The machine turns itself off automatically.
La máquina se apaga automáticamente.

b2_27.note: The team are playing well. (BrE) / The team is playing. (AmE)
b2_27.exp:
Los sustantivos colectivos son un grupo en su conjunto.

• BrE: normalmente en plural. número: The team are playing.
• AmE: normalmente unidades. número: The team is playing.

Frecuente: team, family, government, committee, staff, audience, crew, police, army, public, management
mistakes: The police is here → The police are here (plural en BrE)
The team is playing well - cierto en AmE; are verdaderas en BrE
ex: The government have announced new measures. (BrE)
El gobierno anunció nuevas medidas.
The audience were on their feet. (BrE)
El público se puso de pie de un salto.

b2_28.note: a half, three quarters, 5.7 = five point seven, 25%
b2_28.exp:
Fracciones:½ = a half; ⅓ = a third; ¼ = a quarter; ¾ = three quarters; ⅔ = two thirds.
El numerador es cuantitativo, el denominador es ordinal (plural si el numerador > 1).

Decimales: punto (no coma): 3.14 = three point one four.
Matemáticas: + = plus; - = minus; × = times; ÷ = divided by; = = equals.
mistakes: Two third of students → Two thirds of students
3,14 → 3.14 (punto, no coma)
25 percents → 25 percent (sin s)
ex: Three quarters of students passed the exam.
Tres cuartas partes de los estudiantes aprobaron el examen.
The inflation rate fell to 2.5 percent.
La tasa de inflación cayó al 2,5 por ciento.

b2_29.note: faster, more carefully, best, worse, further
b2_29.exp:
Los adverbios forman grados de comparación según las mismas reglas que los adjetivos.

• Monosilábico: + er/est: fast→faster, hard→harder, early→earlier
• Más en -ly: more/most: carefully→more carefully→most carefully
• Incorrecto: well→better→best, badly→worse→worst, far→further→furthest, little→less→least, much→more→most
mistakes: She sings more beautiful → She sings more beautifully
He runs more fast → He runs faster
She works most hardly → She works hardest
ex: She spoke more confidently than before.
Habló con más confianza que antes.
He works hardest in the team.
Trabaja más duro que nadie en el equipo.

c1_01.note: Never have I seen this. Rarely does she complain.
c1_01.exp:
Para enfatizar, el adverbio/expresión negativo se coloca al principio → verbo auxiliar antes del sujeto (orden de las palabras como en una pregunta).

Palabras que desencadenan la inversión: never, rarely, seldom, little, hardly, scarcely, barely, not only, only, no sooner
mistakes: Never I have seen → Never have I seen (inversión: auxiliar antes de sujeto)
Rarely she complains → Rarely does she complain
ex: Never have I seen anything so beautiful.
Nunca había visto algo tan hermoso.
Rarely does she make a mistake.
Rara vez comete errores.
Little did I know what was coming.
No tenía idea de lo que me esperaba.

c1_02.text: No sólo... sino también con inversión
c1_02.note: Not only did he apologise, but he also offered to help.
c1_02.exp:
No solo + inversión en la primera parte, la segunda parte es el orden habitual.
Usado para énfasis: expresa que algo fue más lejos de lo esperado.
mistakes: Not only he apologised → Not only did he apologise
Not only she is talented but also is hardworking → pero she también es trabajadora (la segunda parte es el orden habitual)
ex: Not only is she talented, but she is also very hard-working.
No sólo es talentosa, sino también muy trabajadora.
Not only did they arrive late, but they also forgot the documents.
No sólo llegaron tarde, sino que también olvidaron sus documentos.

c1_03.text: Apenas / Apenas / Tan pronto como + inversión
c1_03.note: Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang.
c1_03.exp:
Construcciones de secuencia inmediata:
• Apenas/Apenas + tenía + sujeto + V3 + cuando/antes + Pasado simple
• Apenas + tenía + sujeto + V3 + que + Pasado simple
mistakes: Hardly I had sat → Hardly had I sat
No sooner I sat than → No sooner had I sat than
ex: Hardly had she arrived when it started to rain.
Apenas había llegado cuando empezó a llover.
No sooner had I sat down than someone knocked at the door.
Me acababa de sentar cuando alguien llamó a la puerta.

c1_04.text: Inversión en condicionales: Had / Were / Should
c1_04.note: Had I known (= If I had known). Were I you (= If I were you).
c1_04.exp:
Estilo formal: excluye if, utiliza inversión:
• Had + sujeto + V3 = If + Pasado perfecto (tercer tipo)
• Eran + sujeto (+ a + infinitivo) = If + Pasado simple (segundo tipo)
• Debería + sujeto + infinitivo = Si (poco probable, escriba 1)
mistakes: Have I known, I would have helped → Had I known
Should you need help, please to call → please call (sin hacerlo después, por favor)
ex: Had she told me, I would have helped.
Si me lo hubiera dicho, le habría ayudado.
Were I in your position, I would accept.
Si yo fuera usted, estaría de acuerdo.
Should you need assistance, please call us.
Si necesitas ayuda, llámanos.

c1_05.text: It-cleft: It was John who called.
c1_05.note: Para resaltar cualquier miembro de una oración.
c1_05.exp:
Estructura: Eso + ser + elemento seleccionado + quién/ese/cuál + resto
Desvía el foco de atención al elemento resaltado.

• Para personas: who; para cosas/circunstancias - that/which.
mistakes: <s>It was John who he called</s> → It was John who called (extra él)
It was the noise which woke me - correcto, pero that es preferible para las cosas
ex: It was the noise that woke me up. (не шум вообще, именно этот)
Fue el ruido lo que me despertó.
It is hard work that leads to success.
Es el trabajo duro el que conduce al éxito.

c1_06.text: Wh-cleft: What surprised me was the price.
c1_06.note: What I need is rest. What she said shocked everyone.
c1_06.exp:
Estructura: Qué + cláusula subordinada + to be + elemento resaltado
Destaca la importancia del elemento introducido al final.
mistakes: What I love it is London → What I love is London (extra it)
What surprised me were the price → What surprised me was the price (número singular)
ex: What I love about London is the diversity.
Lo que más me gusta de Londres es la diversidad.
What he did was completely unexpected.
Lo que hizo fue completamente inesperado.

c1_07.text: Subjuntivo formal después de verbos de exigencia.
c1_07.note: I suggest he leave. It is vital that she be informed.
c1_07.exp:
