Después de suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose, request, require, ask, advise, order + that - la forma básica del verbo para todas las personas (sin -s, sin was).

La versión británica suele utilizar should en lugar del subjuntivo: I suggest that he should leave.
Americano - a menudo un subjuntivo puro.
mistakes: I suggest that he leaves → Le sugiero que leave (subjuntivo - ¡sin -s!)
It is essential that she is informed → that she be informed
ex: I recommend that he see a doctor.
Le recomiendo que consulte a un médico.
It is essential that all students attend the meeting.
Es esencial que todos los estudiantes asistan a la reunión.

c1_08.note: It's high time you went to bed. It's time we left.
c1_08.exp:
Ya es hora (ya casi) + asunto + Pasado simple
Significado: presente/futuro: estamos hablando de algo que debería haberse hecho hace mucho tiempo.
high time - aún más fuerte: ¡ya es hora!
mistakes: It's high time you will go → It's high time you went (Past Simple!)
It's high time for you go → It's high time you went
ex: It's time she found a new job.
Ya es hora de que encuentre un nuevo trabajo.
It's high time you apologised.
Ya es hora de disculparse.

c1_09.note: She talks as if she knew everything. He looked as though he had seen a ghost.
c1_09.exp:
as if / as though + Past Simple es una comparación poco realista en el presente.
as if / as though + Past Perfect es una comparación poco realista sobre el pasado.
mistakes: She talks as if she knows everything (situación irreal) → as if she knew
He looked as if he seen a ghost → as if he had seen
ex: He spends money as if he were a millionaire.
Gasta dinero como si fuera millonario.
She spoke as though she had met him before.
Ella habló como si lo hubiera conocido antes.

c1_10.note: So do I. Neither does she. So am I.
c1_10.exp:
So + auxiliar + sujeto - acuerdo con lo afirmativo.
Ninguno/Ni + auxiliar + sujeto - acuerdo con lo negativo.
El verbo auxiliar debe coincidir con el tiempo de la oración original.
mistakes: So I do → So do I (auxiliar antes que sujeto)
Neither she does → Neither does she
I love jazz. So she does too → So does she
ex: I love jazz. So does she.
Me encanta el jazz. Ella también.
I haven't been to Rome. Neither have I.
No he estado en Roma. Yo también.

c1_11.text: I think so / I hope so / I'm afraid so
c1_11.note: Will it rain? — I think so. / I hope not.
c1_11.exp:
so reemplaza la cláusula subordinada después de: think, hope, suppose, expect, believe, imagine, be afraid.
Forma negativa: not (¡no so not!).
mistakes: <s>I think so not</s> → I don't think so
I hope so not → I hope not
ex: Will he come? — I think so. / I don't think so.
¿Vendrá? - Creo que sí. / No pienses.
Is it expensive? — I'm afraid so.
¿Es caro? - Me temo que sí.
Is it closed? — I hope not.
¿Cerrado? - Espero que no.

c1_12.note: The man who called is my brother. VS My brother, who called, is a doctor.
c1_12.exp:
Definición: especifica de quién/qué estamos hablando, sin comas. that es posible. El pronombre se puede omitir si es un objeto.

Sin definición: agrega información; se requieren comas. Sólo who/which (¡no that!). No se puede omitir el pronombre.
mistakes: <s>The film that won the Oscar, was brilliant</s> → sin coma (cláusula definitoria)
Avatar, that came out in 2009 → Avatar, which came out (¡no puedes usarlo en uno que no sea definitorio!)
ex: The film that won the Oscar was brilliant. (определяет, о каком фильме речь)
La película que ganó el Oscar fue genial.
Avatar, which came out in 2009, was a huge hit. (доп. факт о и так известном фильме)
Avatar, lanzado en 2009, se convirtió en un gran éxito.

c1_13.note: The company for which I work. The person with whom I spoke.
c1_13.exp:
Estilo formal: preposición + cuál/quién antes de un pronombre relativo.
Equivalente informal: preposición al final de una frase.
whom es la forma objetiva formal de who.
mistakes: <s>The company which I work for it</s> → extra it
The person who I spoke → the person I spoke to / to whom I spoke
ex: The report to which I referred is attached. (формально)
Se adjunta el informe que mencioné.
The report which I referred to is attached. (нейтрально)
The report I referred to is attached. (разговорно)

c1_14.exp:
La nominalización es la conversión de verbos/adjetivos en sustantivos. Un signo de estilo académico y empresarial.

Sufijos principales:
• -tion/-sion: decidir→decisión, discutir→discusión
• -ment: mejorar→mejora, desarrollar→desarrollo
• -ance/-ence: aparecer→apariencia, diferir→diferencia
• -ity: complejo→complejidad, capaz→capacidad
• -ness: feliz→felicidad, consciente→conciencia
mistakes: I made a decision to expand → correcto, pero el estilo es más débil: Our decision to expand (nominalización)
Descubrió un error → His discovery of the error
ex: She decided to expand. → Our decision to expand the company...
Nuestra decisión de expandirnos...
He discovered that... → His discovery of the error...
Su descubrimiento del error...

c1_15.note: The fact that prices increased → The increase in prices...
c1_15.exp:
La nominalización permite:
1. Comprimir información: There was a significant increase in prices.
2. Añadir definiciones: The rapid increase in house prices...
3. Crea un tono formal e impersonal.
mistakes: There was a significantly increase → a significant increase (adjetivo antes de un sustantivo)
The prices' increase → The increase in prices
ex: There has been a significant improvement in air quality.
La calidad del aire ha mejorado significativamente.
His refusal to comment surprised everyone.
Su negativa a comentar sorprendió a todos.

c1_16.note: Walking down the street, I saw an old friend. Having no money, he couldn't buy food.
c1_16.exp:
La frase participial con participio presente (V-ing) reemplaza la cláusula subordinada:
• Simultaneidad: Walking home, I noticed something strange. (= While I was walking home)
• Motivo: Knowing the answer, she raised her hand. (= Because she knew)

⚠️ ¡El sujeto de la frase participial DEBE coincidir con el sujeto de la oración principal!
Error: Walking down the street, the rain started. (la lluvia no cayó en la calle)
mistakes: Walking down the street, the rain started → sujeto ≠ sujeto. Correcto: Walking down the street, I got wet.
Knowing the answer, her hand was raised → el sujeto debe coincidir: Knowing the answer, she raised her hand.
ex: Arriving at the airport, he realised he had forgotten his passport.
Al llegar al aeropuerto se dio cuenta de que había olvidado su pasaporte.
Not knowing what to do, she called her mother.
Sin saber qué hacer, llamó a su madre.

c1_17.text: Frase participial pasado: V3 / Having + V3 clause
c1_17.note: Written in 1815, the novel... Having finished work, she went home.
c1_17.exp:
V3 clause (Participio Pasado) = significado pasivo: Built in 1889, the Eiffel Tower...

Having + V3 = acción completada antes de la principal:
Having read the report, he called a meeting. (= After he had read...)
mistakes: Having read the report, the meeting was called → ¿quién lo leyó? Debería ser: Having read the report, he called a meeting.
Surprised by the news, she was sat down → ella misma: she sat down
ex: Surprised by the news, she sat down silently.
Sorprendida por la noticia, se sentó en silencio.
Having finished the exam, the students left the room.
Una vez finalizado el examen, los alumnos abandonaron el aula.

c2_01.text: Condicional a menos que / siempre / siempre y cuando / con la condición de que
c2_01.note: Unless you study, you'll fail. As long as you're honest, I'll help.
c2_01.exp:
unless = si no (¡pero no se puede usar con negación!): Unless you hurry = If you don't hurry
provided/providing (that) = si y sólo si (condición estricta)
as long as = siempre que (supuesto)
on condition that = con la condición de que (formalmente)
in case = en caso
mistakes: <s>Unless you don't study</s> → Unless you study (a menos que = si no, doble negativo es innecesario)
As long as you'll be honest → As long as you are honest
ex: I'll lend you money, as long as you pay me back.
Te prestaré dinero con la condición de que lo devuelvas.
You can use my laptop, provided you don't download anything.
Puedes usar mi computadora portátil, siempre y cuando no descargues nada.

c2_02.note: Suppose you won the lottery — what would you do?
c2_02.exp:
Suppose/Supposing: se utiliza como if en preguntas hipotéticas.
What if es un análogo informal.

Con Pasado Simple: una situación es improbable o imaginaria.
mistakes: Suppose you would win → Suppose you won (Pasado simple para hipótesis)
ex: Supposing you had to choose — which would you pick?
Imagina que tuvieras que elegir: ¿qué elegirías?
What if nobody comes? What should we do?
¿Qué pasa si nadie viene? ¿Qué debemos hacer?

c2_03.note: Only when I left did I realise. Only then did he understand.
c2_03.exp:
Only + when/after/if/then/by/in/on: todo el grupo se mueve al principio → inversión.

Este es uno de los recursos retóricos más poderosos al escribir y hablar en público.
mistakes: Only when I left, I realised → Only when I left did I realise (¡inversión!)
Only after years of practice, she mastered → ... did she master
ex: Only when you experience it can you truly understand.
Sólo experimentándolo se puede comprender verdaderamente.
Only after years of practice did she master the skill.
Sólo después de años de práctica dominó la habilidad.

c2_04.note: So great was his relief that he wept. Such was her talent...
c2_04.exp:
Libro y estilo oratorio.
So + adj/adv + be/aux + sujeto
Tal + era/eran + sujeto
mistakes: So great his relief was that → So great was his relief
Such great was her talent → Such was her talent / So great was her talent
ex: So rapid was the change that nobody could adapt.
Los cambios ocurrieron tan rápido que nadie pudo adaptarse.
Such was her talent that she was offered a scholarship.
Tan grande era su talento que le ofrecieron una beca.

c2_05.text: Cobertura: appear to, seem to, tend to, be likely to
c2_05.note: Prices appear to be rising. This tends to occur when...
c2_05.exp:
La cobertura es la suavización deliberada de declaraciones para expresar modestia científica.

Estructuras principales:
• appear/seem to - aparentemente
• tend to - como regla general, tiende a
• be likely/unlikely to - probable/improbable
• be thought/considered to be - se cree que
mistakes: Prices appear rising → Prices appear to be rising
Results seem suggest → Results seem to suggest
ex: The results appear to suggest a correlation.
Los resultados parecen indicar una correlación.
Companies tend to underestimate implementation costs.
Las empresas tienden a subestimar los costos de implementación.

c2_06.text: Marcadores del discurso en el texto académico.
c2_06.note: Furthermore, Nevertheless, Conversely, In light of, With regard to
c2_06.exp:
Los marcadores estructuran y conectan el texto académico:

• Adición: Moreover, Furthermore, In addition, Additionally
• Contraste: However, Nevertheless, Nonetheless, Conversely, On the other hand
• Resultado: Therefore, Consequently, As a result, Hence, Thus
• Explicación: In other words, That is to say, Namely
• Concesión: Admittedly, While it is true that, Despite this
mistakes: además/además confusión - ambos suman, pero además es más fuerte
<s>Conversely, this shows the same</s>; por el contrario, introduce contraste, no confirmación.
ex: The experiment failed. Nevertheless, the findings were instructive.
El experimento fracasó. Aún así, los resultados fueron instructivos.
Furthermore, the data suggests a strong correlation.
Además, los datos sugieren una fuerte correlación.

c2_07.text: Registros del habla: formal, neutral, coloquial.
c2_07.note: I would like to enquire... vs I'd like to ask... vs Can I ask...
c2_07.exp:
El registro está determinado por el propósito, la audiencia y el contexto.

Formal: pasiva, nominalización, conjunciones complejas, formas completas, verbos de origen latino (commence, terminate, assist).
Neutral: gramática estándar, sin jerga, abreviaturas moderadas.
Informal: puntos suspensivos, phrasal verbs (put off = postpone), contracciones, expresiones coloquiales.
mistakes: Mezcla de registros: comienzo formal y final coloquial en un mismo texto.
I would like to ask about this thing → this matter (caso formal)
ex: Formal: I wish to draw your attention to a discrepancy.
Neutral: I want to point out a mistake.
Informal: Just wanted to flag something up.

c2_08.text: Connotaciones de sinónimos - matices de significado
c2_08.exp:
Los sinónimos difieren en connotación (coloración emocional) y registro.

Ejemplos de escalas:
• slim (+) → thin (0) → skinny (-) → scrawny/gaunt (--)
• determined (+) → firm (0) → stubborn/pig-headed (-)
• thrifty (+) → economical (0) → stingy/tight-fisted (-)
• confident (+) → assertive (0) → arrogant (-)
mistakes: She is very thin (neutral) versus slim intencional (+) o skinny (−)
Usar una palabra con una connotación incorrecta al hacer un cumplido: stubborn en lugar de determined
ex: She is slim. (+) / She is thin. (0) / She is skinny. (-)
Lo mismo, pero diferente actitud.

c2_09.note: "Lucharemos en las playas, lucharemos en las zonas de desembarco..." - anáfora
c2_09.exp:
Anáfora: repetición de palabras al inicio de frases sucesivas. "I have a dream... I have a dream..."
Quiasmo: estructura cruzada AB-BA. "Ask not what your country can do for you, but what you can do for your country."
Tricolon: tres elementos paralelos. "Veni, vidi, vici." / "Government of the people, by the people, for the people."

Estas técnicas se utilizan en oratoria, ensayo y periodismo.
mistakes: Usar anáfora sin estructura paralela altera el ritmo
Tricolon con elementos desiguales: "fast, efficiently, with great care" → "fast, efficient, and careful"
ex: Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears. (триколон)
The more you learn, the more you earn. (хиазм в народной мудрости)

c2_10.note: conduct research, draw conclusions, reach a consensus, address an issue
c2_10.exp:
En C2 es importante utilizar el verbo "correcto" con cada sustantivo.

Colocaciones académicas:
• conduct/carry out investigación (no make/do)
• draw/reach a conclusion
• raise/address/tackle an issue
• reach/achieve a consensus
• make significant progress
• pose/present a challenge
mistakes: make research → conduct/carry out research
do a conclusion → draw/reach a conclusion
make an issue → raise/address an issue
ex: Researchers conducted extensive interviews.
Los investigadores realizaron extensas entrevistas.
The committee failed to reach a consensus.
El comité no pudo llegar a un consenso.

c2_11.note: Weather permitting, we'll have a picnic. Her eyes filled with tears, she left the room.
c2_11.exp:
Construcción absoluta = sustantivo/pronombre + participio (sujeto independiente).
Usado en estilo escrito y formal: agrega una circunstancia sin conjunción.

Tipos:
• Weather permitting = If the weather permits
• All things considered = If you consider everything
• Her work finished = When/After her work was finished
• This done = When/After this was done
mistakes: <s>Weather permitting, the picnic will be had by us</s> → pasivo redundante
Her eyes filling with tears, she left es aceptable, pero Her eyes filled es más exacto para un hecho completo.
ex: All things considered, it was a successful event.
Considerándolo todo, fue un evento exitoso.
The deadline having passed, the project was cancelled.
Una vez vencido el plazo, el proyecto fue cancelado.

c2_12.text: Elipsis y sustitución en texto conectado.
c2_12.note: I wanted to go but didn't (want to). She said she'd call and she did.
c2_12.exp:
La elipsis es la omisión de elementos ya conocidos.
Sustitución: usar do/so/one/it en lugar de repetir.

Tipos de elipse:
• A: Are you coming? B: Might (do).
• She speaks French and he does too / so does he.
• I wanted to leave, but wasn't allowed to. (leave omitido)

Sustitución: I thought he'd pass. He did. / The big one? I prefer the small one.
mistakes: I wanted to go but didn't want to → but didn't (omitimos querer)
She said she'd call and she said → and she did (sustitución por do)
ex: Can you drive? — I used to (drive).
¿Puedes conducir? - Antes podía hacerlo.
She said she'd be here and she was.
Ella dijo que vendría y vino.

c2_13.text: Frases infinitivas en lugar de cláusulas subordinadas.
c2_13.note: I want you to explain. She asked me to help. He seems to be happy.
c2_13.exp:
El infinitivo complejo (Objeto complejo) reemplaza la cláusula subordinada:
I want + object + to-infinitive: I want her to stay.

Después de see, hear, watch, let, make, have - infinitivo sin to:
I saw her leave. / She made him cry. / Let me help.
En la pasiva - con to: He was made to pay.

Construcciones con seem, appear, happen, prove + to-inf:
She seems to know. / He happened to be there.
mistakes: I saw her to leave → I saw her leave (después de ver sin hacerlo)
<s>She was made to leave</s> - ¡es cierto! En pasivo - con to
I want that she stays → I want her to stay
ex: I need you to sign this document.
Necesito que firmes este documento.
She was made to apologise publicly.
Se vio obligada a disculparse públicamente.
He seemed to have forgotten everything.
Parecía haberlo olvidado todo.

c2_14.text: Future Perfect Continuous: will have been + V-ing
c2_14.note: By next year, I will have been studying English for five years.
c2_14.exp:
Future Perfect Continuous = will have been + V-ing

Énfasis en la duración de una acción que durará hasta cierto punto en el futuro. A menudo responde a la pregunta "¿Cuánto falta para entonces?"

Se usa frecuentemente con by (the time), for, when: By Monday, she will have been working on this project for three weeks.
mistakes: By next year I will been studying → I will have been studying
She will have been work → She will have been working
ex: By next year, I will have been learning English for five years.
El año que viene habré estado estudiando inglés durante cinco años.
When we arrive, she will have been waiting for two hours.
Cuando lleguemos, ya habrá estado esperando durante dos horas.

c2_15.text: Coordinación de tiempos verbales - secuencia de tiempos verbales
c2_15.note: She said she had been working. He thought it would be difficult.
c2_15.exp:
En oraciones complejas, el verbo de la cláusula subordinada concuerda en el tiempo con la principal.

Si el verbo principal está en pasado:
• Present Simple → Past Simple: he said it was true
• Past Simple → Past Perfect: she said she had seen it
• Present Perfect → Past Perfect: he said he had finished
• will → would; can → could; may → might; is → was

⚠️ Excepción: las verdades generales y los hechos científicos no cambian: She said that water boils at 100°C.
mistakes: She said that water is boiling (hecho) → water boils
He said he seen it → He said he had seen it
ex: He told me that he had been living there for years.
Me dijo que había vivido allí durante muchos años.
She said the Earth moves around the Sun. (общая истина — не меняем)
Dijo que la Tierra se mueve alrededor del Sol.

c2_16.text: Conjunciones coordinantes: and, but, or, nor, for, yet, so
c2_16.note: FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So
c2_16.exp:
Las conjunciones coordinantes conectan partes equivalentes de una oración.

Siete Básicos (acrónimo FANBOYS):
• for = porque (formal): She left, for she was tired.
• and = y (sumando)
• nor = y no (Ni/Ni... ¡inversión!): She didn't call, nor did she write.
• but = pero (contraste)
• or = o (alternativa)
• yet = sin embargo (contraste, más formal pero)
• so = por lo tanto (consecuencia)
mistakes: <s>She was tired, yet kept working</s> - correcto sin "ella" en la segunda parte
She didn't call nor she wrote → nor did she write (¡inversión!)
ex: She was tired, yet she kept working.
Estaba cansada, pero siguió trabajando.
He didn't study, nor did he attend class.
No estudiaba ni iba a clases.

c2_17.text: Conjunciones subordinantes: although, whereas, provided, unless...
c2_17.note: although, as though, whereas, provided that, unless, given that, in case
c2_17.exp:
Las conjunciones subordinantes introducen cláusulas subordinadas.

Por valor:
• Tiempo: when, while, as, after, before, until, once, as soon as, whenever
• Razones: because, since, as, given that, seeing that
• Condiciones: if, unless, provided, as long as, in case, supposing
• Metas: so that, in order that, lest
• Concesiones: although, even though, whereas, while, however
mistakes: Although the rain, we went → Although it was raining
<s>Seeing that the deadline passed</s> → had passed (Pasado perfecto ante otro pasado)
ex: Seeing that the deadline had passed, we cancelled the meeting.
Como pasó la fecha límite, cancelamos la reunión.
Lest she forget, he sent her a reminder.
Para que ella no lo olvidara, le envió un recordatorio.

c2_18.text: Coma, punto y coma y dos puntos
c2_18.note: Use a comma before FANBOYS. Use a semicolon to link related clauses.
c2_18.exp:
Coma:
• Antes de coordinar conjunciones FANBOYS entre cláusulas independientes.
• Después de palabras/cambios de frase introductorios: However, she decided to stay.
• En las enumeraciones (coma de Oxford - antes del último y): apples, oranges, and bananas.

Punto y coma (;): conecta dos cláusulas independientes sin conjunción.
She was tired; she went to bed.

Dos puntos (:): introduce una lista, explicación, cita.
mistakes: However she decided to stay → However, she decided
She was tired; and she went to bed → sin conjunción después del punto y coma: She was tired; she went to bed.
ex: However, the results were inconclusive; further research is required.
Sin embargo, los resultados son mixtos; se requiere más investigación.
The company has three priorities: efficiency, innovation, and sustainability.
La empresa tiene tres prioridades: eficiencia, innovación y sostenibilidad.

c2_19.note: Em dash — for emphasis — sets off a phrase. It's vs its. "Direct speech"
c2_19.exp:
Guión (—): resalta la construcción de un complemento (más fuerte que una coma): The solution — though expensive — proved effective.

Apóstrofe:
• Abreviaturas: it's = it is; don't; they're
• Caso posesivo: John's book; the students' results
• ⚠️ its (pertenencia) vs it's (es)

Citas: AmE - doble ("text"), BrE - simple ('text').
mistakes: Its a big house → It's a big house
The cats tail → The cat's tail
Her's book → Her book (los pronombres posesivos no tienen apóstrofe)
ex: The project — launched in 2020 — exceeded all expectations.
El proyecto, lanzado en 2020, superó todas las expectativas.
It's important to check its settings before use.
Es importante comprobar su configuración antes de usarlo.

c2_20.text: Preguntas especiales e indirectas en texto académico.
c2_20.note: The question is whether... / I wonder what the data shows.
c2_20.exp:
En los textos académicos las preguntas directas se sustituyen por otras indirectas (cláusulas interrogativas).

Una pregunta indirecta es una cláusula subordinada con el orden habitual de las palabras (sin inversión, sin hacer).

Palabras introductorias: si, si (sí/no), qué, dónde, cuándo, cómo, por qué, cuál.

Ejemplo: What does this data show? → The question is what this data shows.
mistakes: I wonder what does the data show → what the data shows (sin inversión en una pregunta indirecta)
The question is whether does he know → whether he knows
ex: I wonder whether the hypothesis is correct.
Me pregunto si la hipótesis es cierta.
The study examines how social media affects behaviour.
El estudio examina cómo las redes sociales influyen en el comportamiento.
